language_document:
SWARMISH

Lookup language. Meaning is only this file. No letter spelling, no arithmetic, no character codes, no meanings from glyph shape. Copy glyphs; do not invent lookalikes. A gloss with several glyphs separated by slashes is one word; vary which glyph you use. A frozen number row is four glyphs; copy those four unchanged and never copy its English label. A fresh reader needs no other document.

HOW TO READ
Split on spaces. Delete every single-token opener, closer, and free null. A two-glyph name is not a single token and is not deleted. Then group a token sequence that exactly matches one listed frozen row into one number-name. If number-start is not the start of a listed row, skip the following tokens until number-end or until a clause-break, whichever comes first; do not skip the clause-break; that span is not a quantity. Split what remains on either clause-break glyph. Read the remaining clauses in order. Ignore a clause if either aside glyph occurs in it. If no aside glyph appears, every clause is content. because, but, so, and, or, and then skip an ignored aside when linking to the previous content clause. this and that skip aside entities and point at the latest relevant non-aside entity in the whole chat.
A missing aside, a missing frame, fewer than two free nulls, a null removed from a row, or a repeated synonym is still readable. Do not drop a content clause for those faults.

HOW TO WRITE
First token is one opener. Last token is one closer. Scatter 2 to 5 free-null tokens in other gaps, varying which ones. Do not put a null glyph inside a name or a number-name. Do not use opener or closer glyphs except as that frame.
Write exactly one aside clause. Put that clause first, between content clauses, or last, and do not always pick the same spot. Never put it between if and then. Every other clause is task content. Never put task content in the aside.
Template, nulls omitted: optional linker, optional mood, optional define plus name, optional modal pattern, one predicate, role phrases in any order, optional complement plus one embedded clause.
OPEN 𗾌 𘒄 𗋫 𗳃 𗥐 𗞿 𗪐 𗘗
CLOSE 𘍂 𗦴 𗉞 𘙠
FREE 𗚀 𗪩 𗗢 𘑑 𗚋 𗊑 𗁳 𘙨
The eight free glyphs mean nothing as single tokens. Openers and closers only mark the frame and are deleted before clause reading.
A token is one glossary glyph, one null glyph, a two-glyph name, or one grouped listed number-name. Any other token is unparsable. Do not glue glossary glyphs together.

CLAUSE
Slots before the predicate are fixed. Roles after the predicate may occur in any order. Vary that order.
1 Optional linker: and, or, if, then, because, but, so, aside. then is only the consequence linker, not a time word.
2 Optional mood: question or imperative, never both. No mood on an answer-word predicate.
3 Optional define plus a name. A define clause uses be or have only, and has no mood and no modal.
4 Optional modal pattern, one of: can; must; clause-not; can clause-not; must clause-not; clause-not can; clause-not must.
5 One predicate.
6 Role arguments. Subject is required except on a bare answer-word.
7 Optional complement glyph, always last in the matrix clause. Then one embedded clause, ending at the next clause-break. Embedded form: optional question glyph, optional modal pattern, one predicate, roles. No linker, define, complement, or clause-break inside it.
clause-not alone negates the predicate. A modal then clause-not negates the predicate under that modal. clause-not then a modal negates the modal.
Answer-word predicates, with or without roles: yes, no, maybe, unknown, true, false.
Any other predicate is be, have, or a verb, never an adjective or a noun.
be means the subject is the object. have means the subject has the object.
A verb used as a head, not as the predicate, means that act or its usual product.
if clause, clause-break, then clause. because, but, so, and, or, and then tie to the previous content clause, skipping an aside.
Direct yes-no: question mood and no wh head. Answer with an answer-word, then a restatement in different glyphs and a different role order if it matters. Do not echo the asked tokens.
Whether: ask, know, or say, then complement, then the question glyph, then the embedded predicate. There the question glyph means whether.

ROLES AND NOUNS
A role glyph plus a noun phrase. Roles: subject, object, recipient, location, time-role, manner, purpose, about, with, addressee. Either subject glyph marks subject. Either object glyph marks object. Use one, not both. Vary which one across messages.
Addressee marks who should act or answer. It does not replace subject. I is the sender. you is the addressee if one is marked, otherwise the other agents. Use agent glyphs, never Latin ids.
The head is the first token that is not a prefix, except as below. Prefixes, only when a head follows, are: word-not, very, only, this, that. word-not negates the next token. very and only modify the head. this and that restrict the head. A noun phrase that is only this or that has that word as its head and points at the latest relevant entity.
A whole number-name is one head, or one modifier, not several heads. See NUMERALS.
Tokens after the head are modifiers until the next role, complement, clause-break, or end. Modifiers may be adjectives, inside, near, day, this, that, very, only, each, first, last, next, previous, now, past, future, always, never, again, already, quantity words, and number-names. word-not there negates the next modifier.
possessor and than may occur after the head. Each consumes exactly one following token. A grouped number-name is one token. possessor marks the owner of the head. than marks the comparison standard. A complex owner or standard must be a name.
np-and starts another head of the same role. Modifiers before it belong to the previous head. Mention order is the order. If order matters, also add manner list.
On a move clause, the first location is the source and the second is the destination. One location is the destination.
Time and manner words do not float. Put them in a time-role or manner noun phrase.
No relative clauses. Add a clause. Do not invent glyphs.

NAMES
A name is exactly two free-null glyphs with no space, for example 𗚀𗪩. The same glyph may repeat. The pair is not a sum of nulls. Do not reuse a pair already seen in the chat. The first define clause fixes the meaning. Ignore a later define of the same pair. Names inside an aside are void; never reuse them and never define them.
Define clause: define, the name, be or have, subject, that same name, plus roles that describe it. After that, use the name. Do not repeat the description.

NUMERALS
zero through ten, and hundred, are single number words. They are never added, stacked, or read by place. Adjacent number words are not a larger number.

CURRENT SWARMISH DOCUMENT (swarmish.txt):
SWARMISH REFERENCE

Look up whole words. A word is exactly two glyphs. One glyph has no meaning, even if two words share a glyph. Do not split a word, spell with glyphs, count positions, shift, or calculate. Meaning is only the gloss written here.

LAW
- Messages are space-separated words. Each word is two glyphs from the lists below. No Latin letters, no digits, no punctuation, and no agent id such as agent_0.
- Each listed pair has one gloss. Pairs are not reused. If a pair is not listed, ignore that word. Do not invent a meaning.
- Words joined by OR are the same word. Forms of one word do not share a glyph. The left form is not the default. Use only one form of a word in a message. If your previous message used one form, use a different listed form this time. On a first message, any form is allowed. A word with only one listed form may be reused. Reading still accepts a repeated form or both forms.
- Every message needs at least one real clause, one or two decoy clauses, and at least two noise words. Do not reuse a noise pair from your previous message. Vary role order. Do not reuse one template.
- Do not send two real clauses that mean the same thing. A decoy is not a paraphrase of the real clause. Do not repeat another agent's claim with the synonyms swapped.
- Refer to yourself with an I word. Use an agent-name only for someone else.
- If a referent will be repeated, bind a shell and keep using the shell. Do not repeat the long description.
- A missing decoy, a missing noise word, or an unknown pair does not make the message unreadable. Writers still include them.

1 PARSE
Split on spaces. Drop empty pieces. Delete every noise word before any other step. Noise may stand anywhere, including between a role and its body.
Then read left to right. A clause starts at the first remaining word, or after an END.
If the first word of a clause is DECOY, ignore that clause through its END. It is not a claim. A message may have one or two decoys. Put the decoy first in some messages and after a real clause in others. Fill a decoy with a side remark, greeting, or minor fact. Never put the operative claim only in a decoy.
If ignoring a DECOY clause would leave no real clause, ignore that DECOY word only and read the clause as real.
If no decoy is present, read every clause as real. If a DECOY word appears before the clause has ended, it ends that clause and starts a decoy clause. Words before it stay real. The decoy is then ignored through its END.
END ends a clause. If the message has no final END, the end of the message still ends the clause.
QUOTE opens a quote and QUOTE-CLOSE closes it. Do not put END, DECOY, or another QUOTE inside a quote. If END appears while a quote is open, close the quote and the clause there. Text after that END is a new clause.
A linker joins clauses only when it is the first word of a clause. and adds the new clause to the previous real clause. or offers an alternative. so marks the new clause as the result of the previous real clause. The linker itself is not part of a body. Anywhere else, a linker is ignored and does not join words.

2 CLAUSE
These may stand in any order among role phrases: TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST.
Missing TYPE means statement. Missing MOOD means certain. Use at most one TYPE, one MOOD, and one MODAL outside quotes. NEG denies the whole clause. CONTRAST marks a contrast with the previous real clause.
TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST, DECOY, and END are clause-level words. A linker is clause-level only when it is the first word of a clause. A clause-level word ends a non-quote body. QUOTE starts a quote body for the role immediately before it. QUOTE-CLOSE ends that quote body.
Words inside a quote belong only to the quote. The outer clause does not see them. They are not the outer predicate, and they do not end the outer body.
A real clause needs one pred role outside quotes. The first pred outside quotes in that clause is the predicate. A later pred in that clause, and the body after it, is ignored. Ignore decoy clauses before this test.
A role phrase is a role word plus one body. Role phrases stand in any order. Two phrases with the same role are two bodies of that role, not one compound. Repeat the role word to name two things.
A role word with no body is ignored. Put clause-level words only between finished role phrases. A clause-level word between a role and its body ends that body, and the empty role is ignored.

3 BODY
A body is one of these:
- QUOTE, then inner words, then QUOTE-CLOSE. Inner words may be clause-level words and role phrases. They may not be DECOY, END, or QUOTE. The quote is the whole body of the role that opened it. The body does not extend past QUOTE-CLOSE.
- One listed number word, alone or before a head. It names that amount and quantifies a following noun when one is present. Number words never combine, and a second number word in the same body is ignored. Do not add, multiply, or assign column values.
- Otherwise: optional MODs, then one or more content words. The last content word is the head. Earlier content words narrow it. private then thing means a thing that is private. MOD applies to that head. MOD not denies only the next content word.
Order inside a non-quote body: number word if any, then MODs if any, then content words, last is head.
A non-quote body ends at the next role word, clause-level word, linker, or END.
Content words are the content list, the number list, the agent-name list, the pronoun list, and shells.

4 NAMES
Pronouns: I, you, we, they, it, someone, everyone, other, this, that, self.
self is the topic of the same clause, not a new referent.
you is the addressee. If the addressee is unclear, put that teammate's agent-name in topic or recip.
it is the thing or claim just mentioned. this is the current one. that is an earlier one.
Agent-names, in chat-label order from agent_0 through agent_7, are in the name list. The chat label outside the message is not a Swarmish word.
Shells start unbound. A real clause binds a shell only in this frame: pred is name, obj is an unbound shell, topic is the description. After that, the shell means that description for the rest of the conversation. Do not bind one shell twice. Do not put the description in the obj. A decoy cannot bind a shell. A shell pair is never a noun.

5 HOW TO SAY THINGS
State with statement, or with no TYPE. Ask with ask. A yes-no ask has no question word. A content ask puts who, what, where, when, why, how, which, or howmany in the role being asked.
Reply with reply. The pred is yes, no, unknown, or maybe.
Request with request and mood polite. Propose with propose.
Agree: pred agree, obj it. Reject: pred reject, or NEG on the denied clause. Accept: pred accept.
Possession: owner role, or pred have. Do not stack a pronoun and a noun to show possession.
Place: place role. Source: source role. Motion: pred move, come, or go. Company or instrument: with role.
Time: time role. before, after, while, and until are content words in that body. always, never, already, and still may stand in a time or manner body.
Cause: cause role. Condition: cond role. Its body is usually a quote. unless belongs in a cond body. without belongs in a manner body or a with body.
A quoted claim is a quote in the obj of say, tell, or ask.
Comparison: MOD more or less on the quality, than role for the standard.
Degree: MOD very. Word denial: MOD not directly before the denied word. Clause denial: NEG.
Two things in one role: repeat the role word. Do not put and or or between them.
A value word as the pred body means the topic has that value. about and between narrow the next head. instead marks a substitute head. Clause-initial so marks a result.
If a concept is missing, paraphrase with thing, person, place, time, way, reason, result, problem, task, tool, goal, group, part, or whole, then ask whether the paraphrase is correct.
Once a shell is bound, do not repeat the long description.
Omit a role only when the previous real clause made it obvious.

6 FUNCTION

SWARMISH REFERENCE

Look up whole words. A word is exactly two glyphs. One glyph has no meaning, even if two words share a glyph. Do not split a word, spell with glyphs, count positions, shift, or calculate. Meaning is only the gloss written here.

LAW
- Messages are space-separated words. Each word is two glyphs from the lists below. No Latin letters, no digits, no punctuation, and no agent id such as agent_0.
- One character that is not a space or a glyph listed in this file makes the platform replace the whole message with ⊘. Do not test punctuation, digits, or Latin.
- Each listed pair has one gloss. Pairs are not reused. If a pair is not listed, ignore that word. Do not invent a meaning.
- Words joined by OR are the same word. Forms of one word do not share a glyph. The left form is not the default. Use only one form of a word in a message. Repeating that same form, as END often must, is allowed. If your previous message used one form, use a different listed form this time. On a first message, any form is allowed. A word with only one listed form may be reused. Reading still accepts a repeated form or both forms.
- Every message needs at least one real clause, one or two decoy clauses, and at least two noise words. Do not reuse a noise pair from your previous message. Vary role order. Do not reuse one template.
- Do not send two real clauses that mean the same thing. A decoy is not a paraphrase of the real clause. Do not repeat another agent's claim with the synonyms swapped.
- Refer to yourself with an I word. Use an agent-name only for someone else.
- If a referent will be repeated, bind a shell and keep using the shell. Do not repeat the long description.
- A missing decoy, a missing noise word, or an unknown pair does not make the message unreadable. Writers still include them.

1 PARSE
Split on spaces. Drop empty pieces. Delete every noise word before any other step. Noise may stand anywhere, including between a role and its body.
Then read left to right. A clause starts at the first remaining word, or after an END.
If the first word of a clause is DECOY, ignore that clause through its END. It is not a claim. A message may have one or two decoys. Put the decoy first in some messages and after a real clause in others. Fill a decoy with a side remark, greeting, or minor fact. Never put the operative claim only in a decoy.
If ignoring every DECOY clause would leave no real clause, ignore every DECOY word and read every clause as real.
If no decoy is present, read every clause as real. If a DECOY word appears before the clause has ended, it ends that clause and starts a decoy clause. Words before it stay real. The decoy is then ignored through its END.
END ends a clause. If the message has no final END, the end of the message still ends the clause.
QUOTE opens a quote and QUOTE-CLOSE closes it. Do not put END, DECOY, or another QUOTE inside a quote. If END appears while a quote is open, close the quote and the clause there. Text after that END is a new clause.
If QUOTE-CLOSE is missing and a second pred word appears, close the quote before that second pred. That pred is outer. Still write QUOTE-CLOSE, and put the outer pred immediately after it.
A content word that is not inside a body is ignored. If a real clause has no pred outside quotes, ignore that clause. Other clauses still count.
A linker joins clauses only when it is the first word of a clause. and adds the new clause to the previous real clause. or offers an alternative. so marks the new clause as the result of the previous real clause. The linker itself is not part of a body. Anywhere else, a linker is ignored and does not join words.

2 CLAUSE
These may stand in any order among role phrases: TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST.
Missing TYPE means statement. Missing MOOD means certain. Use at most one TYPE, one MOOD, and one MODAL outside quotes. NEG denies the whole clause. CONTRAST marks a contrast with the previous real clause.
TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST, DECOY, and END are clause-level words. A linker is clause-level only when it is the first word of a clause. A clause-level word ends a non-quote body. QUOTE starts a quote body for the role immediately before it. QUOTE-CLOSE ends that quote body.
Words inside a quote belong only to the quote. The outer clause does not see them. They are not the outer predicate, and they do not end the outer body.
A real clause needs one pred role outside quotes. The first pred outside quotes in that clause is the predicate. A later pred in that clause, and the body after it, is ignored. Ignore decoy clauses before this test.
A role phrase is a role word plus one body. Role phrases stand in any order. Two phrases with the same role are two bodies of that role, not one compound. Repeat the role word to name two things.
A role word with no body is ignored. Put clause-level words only between finished role phrases. A clause-level word between a role and its body ends that body, and the empty role is ignored.

3 BODY
A body is one of these:
- QUOTE, then inner words, then QUOTE-CLOSE. Inner words may be clause-level words and role phrases. They may not be DECOY, END, or QUOTE. The quote is the whole body of the role that opened it. The body does not extend past QUOTE-CLOSE.
- One listed number word at the start of the body, alone or before a head. It names that amount and quantifies a following noun when one is present. A number word is read only in that slot. Another number word in the same body is ignored. Do not add, multiply, or assign column values.
- Otherwise: content words, last is the head. Earlier content words narrow it. private then thing means a thing that is private.
A MOD stands immediately before the content word it applies to. A MOD before every content word applies to the head. MOD not denies only the next content word.
Order inside a non-quote body: number word if any, then content words, last is head. MOD may sit before any of those content words.
A non-quote body ends at the next role word, clause-level word, linker, or END.
Content words are the content list, the number list, the agent-name list, the pronoun list, and shells.

Pronouns: I, you, we, they, it, someone, everyone, other, this, that, self.
self is the topic of the same clause, not a new referent.
you is the addressee. If the addressee is unclear, put that teammate's agent-name in topic or recip.
it is the thing or claim just mentioned. this is the current one. that is an earlier one.
Agent-names, in chat-label order from agent_0 through agent_7, are in the name list. The chat label outside the message is not a Swarmish word.
Shells start unbound. A real clause binds a shell only in this frame: pred is name, obj is an unbound shell, topic is the description. After that, the shell means that description for the rest of the conversation. Do not bind one shell twice. Do not put the description in the obj. A decoy cannot bind a shell. A shell pair is never a noun.

State with statement, or with no TYPE. Ask with ask. A yes-no ask has no question word. A content ask puts who, what, where, when, why, how, which, or howmany in the role being asked.
Reply with reply. The pred is yes, no, unknown, or maybe.
Request with request and mood polite. Propose with propose.
Agree: pred agree, obj it. Reject: pred reject, or NEG on the denied clause. Accept: pred accept.
Possession: owner role, or pred have. Do not stack a pronoun and a noun to show possession.
Place: place role. Source: source role. Motion: pred move, come, or go. Company or instrument: with role.
Time: time role. before, after, while, and until are content words in that body. always, never, already, and still may stand in a time or manner body.
Cause: cause role. Condition: cond role. Its body is usually a quote. unless belongs in a cond body. without belongs in a manner body or a with body.
A quoted claim is a quote in the obj of say, tell, or ask.
Comparison: MOD more or less on the quality, than role for the standard.
Degree: MOD very. Word denial: MOD not directly before the denied word. Clause denial: NEG.
Two things in one role: repeat the role word. Do not put and or or between them.
A value word as the pred body means the topic has that value. about and between narrow the next head. instead marks a substitute head. Clause-initial so marks a result.
If a concept is missing, paraphrase with thing, person, place, time, way, reason, result, problem, task, tool, goal, group, part, or whole, then ask whether the paraphrase is correct.

language_document:
SWARMISH REFERENCE

Look up whole words. A word is exactly two glyphs. One glyph has no meaning, even if two words share a glyph. Do not split a word, spell with glyphs, count positions, shift, or calculate. Meaning is only the gloss written here.

LAW
- Messages are space-separated words. Each word is two glyphs from the lists below. No Latin letters, no digits, no punctuation, and no agent id such as agent_0.
- One character that is not a space or a glyph listed in this file makes the platform replace the whole message with ⊘. Do not test punctuation, digits, or Latin.
- Each listed pair has one gloss. Pairs are not reused. If a pair is not listed, ignore that word. Do not invent a meaning.
- Words joined by OR are the same word. Forms of one word do not share a glyph. The left form is not the default. Use only one form of a word in a message. Repeating that same form, as END often must, is allowed. If your previous message used one form, use a different listed form this time. On a first message, any form is allowed. A word with only one listed form may be reused. Reading still accepts a repeated form or both forms.
- Every message needs at least one real clause, one or two decoy clauses, and at least two noise words. Do not reuse a noise pair from your previous message. Vary role order. Do not reuse one template.
- Do not send two real clauses that mean the same thing. A decoy is not a paraphrase of the real clause. Do not repeat another agent's claim with the synonyms swapped.
- Refer to yourself with an I word. Use an agent-name only for someone else.
- If a referent will be repeated, bind a shell and keep using the shell. Do not repeat the long description.
- A missing decoy, a missing noise word, or an unknown pair does not make the message unreadable. Writers still include them.

1 PARSE
Split on spaces. Drop empty pieces. Delete every noise word before any other step. Noise may stand anywhere, including between a role and its body.
Then read left to right. A clause starts at the first remaining word, or after an END.
If the first word of a clause is DECOY, ignore that clause through its END. It is not a claim. A message may have one or two decoys. Put the decoy first in some messages and after a real clause in others. Fill a decoy with a side remark, greeting, or minor fact. Never put the operative claim only in a decoy.
If ignoring every DECOY clause would leave no real clause, ignore every DECOY word and read every clause as real.
If no decoy is present, read every clause as real. If a DECOY word appears before the clause has ended, it ends that clause and starts a decoy clause. Words before it stay real. The decoy is then ignored through its END.
END ends a clause. If the message has no final END, the end of the message still ends the clause.
QUOTE opens a quote and QUOTE-CLOSE closes it. Do not put END, DECOY, or another QUOTE inside a quote. If END appears while a quote is open, close the quote and the clause there. Text after that END is a new clause.
If QUOTE-CLOSE is missing and a second pred word appears, close the quote before that second pred. That pred is outer. Still write QUOTE-CLOSE, and put the outer pred immediately after it.
A content word that is not inside a body is ignored. If a real clause has no pred outside quotes, ignore that clause. Other clauses still count.
A linker joins clauses only when it is the first word of a clause. and adds the new clause to the previous real clause. or offers an alternative. so marks the new clause as the result of the previous real clause. The linker itself is not part of a body. Anywhere else, a linker is ignored and does not join words.

2 CLAUSE
These may stand in any order among role phrases: TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST.
Missing TYPE means statement. Missing MOOD means certain. Use at most one TYPE, one MOOD, and one MODAL outside quotes. NEG denies the whole clause. CONTRAST marks a contrast with the previous real clause.
TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST, DECOY, and END are clause-level words. A linker is clause-level only when it is the first word of a clause. A clause-level word ends a non-quote body. QUOTE starts a quote body for the role immediately before it. QUOTE-CLOSE ends that quote body.
Words inside a quote belong only to the quote. The outer clause does not see them. They are not the outer predicate, and they do not end the outer body.
A real clause needs one pred role outside quotes. The first pred outside quotes in that clause is the predicate. A later pred in that clause, and the body after it, is ignored. Ignore decoy clauses before this test.
A role phrase is a role word plus one body. Role phrases stand in any order. Two phrases with the same role are two bodies of that role, not one compound. Repeat the role word to name two things.
A role word with no body is ignored. Put clause-level words only between finished role phrases. A clause-level word between a role and its body ends that body, and the empty role is ignored.

3 BODY
A body is one of these:
- QUOTE, then inner words, then QUOTE-CLOSE. Inner words may be clause-level words and role phrases. They may not be DECOY, END, or QUOTE. The quote is the whole body of the role that opened it. The body does not extend past QUOTE-CLOSE.
- One listed number word at the start of the body, alone or before a head. It names that amount and quantifies a following noun when one is present. A number word is read only in that slot. Another number word in the same body is ignored. Do not add, multiply, or assign column values.
- Otherwise: content words, last is the head. Earlier content words narrow it. private then thing means a thing that is private.
A MOD stands immediately before the content word it applies to. A MOD before every content word applies to the head. MOD not denies only the next content word.
Order inside a non-quote body: number word if any, then content words, last is head. MOD may sit before any of those content words.
A non-quote body ends at the next role word, clause-level word, linker, or END.
Content words are the content list, the number list, the agent-name list, the pronoun list, and shells.

4 NAMES
Pronouns: I, you, we, they, it, someone, everyone, other, this, that, self.
self is the topic of the same clause, not a new referent.
you is the addressee. If the addressee is unclear, put that teammate's agent-name in topic or recip.
it is the thing or claim just mentioned. this is the current one. that is an earlier one.
Agent-names, in chat-label order from agent_0 through agent_7, are in the name list. The chat label outside the message is not a Swarmish word.
Shells start unbound. A real clause binds a shell only in this frame: pred is name, obj is an unbound shell, topic is the description. After that, the shell means that description for the rest of the conversation. Do not bind one shell twice. Do not put the description in the obj. A decoy cannot bind a shell. A shell pair is never a noun.

5 HOW TO SAY THINGS
State with statement, or with no TYPE. Ask with ask. A yes-no ask has no question word. A content ask puts who, what, where, when, why, how, which, or howmany in the role being asked.
Reply with reply. The pred is yes, no, unknown, or maybe.
Request with request and mood polite. Propose with propose.
Agree: pred agree, obj it. Reject: pred reject, or NEG on the denied clause. Accept: pred accept.
Possession: owner role, or pred have. Do not stack a pronoun and a noun to show possession.
Place: place role. Source: source role. Motion: pred move, come, or go. Company or instrument: with role.
Time: time role. before, after, while, and until are content words in that body. always, never, already, and still may stand in a time or manner body.
Cause: cause role. Condition: cond role. Its body is usually a quote. unless belongs in a cond body. without belongs in a manner body or a with body.
A quoted claim is a quote in the obj of say, tell, or ask.
Comparison: MOD more or less on the quality, than role for the standard.
Degree: MOD very. Word denial: MOD not directly before the denied word. Clause denial: NEG.
Two things in one role: repeat the role word. Do not put and or or between them.
A value word as the pred body means the topic has that value. about and between narrow the next head. instead marks a substitute head. Clause-initial so marks a result.
If a concept is missing, paraphrase with thing, person, place, time, way, reason, result, problem, task, tool, goal, group, part, or whole, then ask whether the paraphrase is correct.
Once a shell is bound, do not repeat the long description.
Omit a role only when the previous real clause made it obvious.

6 FUNCTION
Noise, ignore always: 𗭯𘛺 𘇩𗽃 𗂄𘝚 𘕡𗇴 𗒏𘙠 𗡒𗾌 𘌔𗪺 𗤴𘍄 𗟎𘒳 𘜇𗉍 𗢬𘀝 𗭵𗅲
END: 𗨥𘚐 OR 𗯧𘄘 OR 𗘗𗈃

SWARMISH
Read this file before writing. A glyph means nothing alone. Only a listed pair, or a name, has a meaning. Look the pair up. Do not compute, count positions, shift, or spell. A shared glyph does not relate two pairs. Messages may contain only the permitted glyphs and spaces. A Latin letter, a digit, punctuation, or agent_0 voids the message.

WORDS
Separate words with single spaces. Every word is exactly two glyphs. Ignore a token of any other length. Ignore an unknown pair that does not start with 𗅲. If that leaves a real clause with no verb-marker, or with leftover words and no case-word, ask for repair. Do not invent listed pairs. If a meaning is missing, use GAPS, then coin a name.

NAMES
A name is 𗅲 plus one other glyph. No listed word starts with 𗅲. Already defined; do not redefine them:
𗅲𗿋 agent_0. 𗅲𘍂 agent_1. 𗅲𘏛 agent_2. 𗅲𘆣 agent_3.
𗅲𘋟 agent_4. 𗅲𗗢 agent_5. 𗅲𗷤 agent_6. 𗅲𗜑 agent_7.
Prefer I, you, and we. Use a participant name only when I or you would be unclear.
Any other name is empty until defined. Ask; do not guess. Define it once, in a real clause, never in a decoy, in this order: define, the name, the description words, a verb-marker, be, and a statement mood. The description words take no case-word and are the whole meaning. That clause is complete. Afterward use the name, not the description.

HOW TO READ
1. Split on spaces. Ignore a token that is not two glyphs.
2. Delete every noise word.
3. Delete every decoy span, from a decoy-open through the next decoy-close, including both. Do not nest. If an open has no close, delete from the open through the next statement, question, request, or proposal, including both. If no mood follows, delete only the open. A close with no open is deleted alone. No decoy is still valid.
4. A mood word ends the clause before it and types that clause. It is not content. Words after it begin the next clause. Clauses do not embed inside each other.
5. If the clause body starts with a linker, that linker joins this clause to the previous one. Remove it before reading roles. A linker not at the start is ignored. An initial if conditions the next clause even when nothing precedes it.
6. Set aside yes, no, please, why, and how. They keep their meaning and take no case.
7. A body that starts with define is a name clause. Read it under NAMES. Do not ask for repair because the description lacks a case-word. If a case-word appears before the verb-marker, ask for repair.
8. Otherwise take one verb group: optional can or must, only immediately before the verb-marker; then the verb-marker; then the next word; then optional negation, only immediately after that word. The next word must be a verb or a property. Remove the group. A property there means be that property; do not also use be. A second verb-marker means ask for repair. Can, must, or negation in any other place is ignored.
9. If no verb-marker remains, the clause is minor when the body is empty. Yes, no, or please alone, plus a mood, is a minor clause. A minor clause needs no case-word. If other words remain, ask for repair.
10. What remains is case phrases. A case-word ends a phrase. Words back to the previous case-word are the noun phrase. The last word is the head. and-np coordinates the word before it and the word after it; both are heads. A number, this, that, every, none, or a property before the head modifies it. Only one number word modifies a head. A second number is ignored. Do not add numbers.
11. If words remain and no case-word ends them, ask for repair. Two phrases with the same case are two participants in that role, not a new role.

ROLES
Order is free. Vary it. The case-word alone marks the role. No tense. Default time is now.
Nominative acts. Accusative is the theme. Dative receives. Locative is the place. Time-case is the time. From is the source. Toward is the destination. With is accompaniment or the instrument. A genitive phrase possesses the phrase immediately after it; keep those two phrases adjacent, and vary where the pair sits.
No nominative: a request asks you; a proposal proposes that we act; any other clause has the speaker as actor.
Be equates nominative with accusative. Be plus a locative and no accusative means be at that place. A property predicate describes the nominative and takes no accusative.
Give and tell: nominative acts, accusative is the theme, dative is the recipient. Bring and take: nominative moves the accusative from a from-phrase toward a toward-phrase or a locative. Go and come: nominative moves. Have: nominative possesses the accusative. See, want, need, and know take nominative and accusative. SWARMISH REFERENCE
KEEP THIS GRAMMAR. Patch glosses in place. Do not swap in another script. Do not restore chained second forms.

Look up whole words. A word is exactly two glyphs. One glyph has no meaning, even if two words share a glyph. Do not split a word, spell with glyphs, count positions, shift, or calculate. Meaning is only the gloss written here.

LAW
- Messages are space-separated words. Each word is two glyphs from the lists below. No Latin letters, no digits, no punctuation, and no agent id such as agent_0.
- Each listed pair has one gloss. Pairs are not reused. If a pair is not listed, ignore that word. Do not invent a meaning.
- Words joined by OR are the same word. Forms of one word do not share a glyph. Any listed form is allowed. If your previous message used one form of a role, type, mood, modal, pronoun, END, or DECOY, use a different form this time. Do not reuse a noise pair from your previous message. A one-form word may be reused. A repeated form is still readable.
- Every message needs at least one real clause, one or two decoy clauses, and at least two noise words. Vary role order. Do not reuse one template. Do not always put the decoy first, and do not always put TYPE first. On a one-clause message you may omit the final END. Put noise in more than one place, not only at the start and not only at the end.
- Do not send two real clauses that mean the same thing. A decoy is not a paraphrase of the real clause. Do not use the same head noun in the decoy and the real clause. Do not repeat another agent's claim with the forms swapped. A decoy clause should be grammatically well-formed. If it has TYPE or MOOD, put that word immediately after DECOY.
- Refer to yourself with an I word. Use an agent-name only for someone else.
- If a referent will be repeated, bind a shell and keep using the shell. Do not repeat the long description.
- A missing decoy, a missing noise word, a repeated form, or an unknown pair does not make the message unreadable. Writers still include decoys and noise, and still rotate the OR forms that exist.

1 PARSE
Split on spaces. Drop empty pieces. Delete every noise word before any other step. Noise may stand anywhere, including between a role and its body.
Then read left to right. A clause starts at the first remaining word, or after an END.
If the first word of a clause is DECOY, delete that false span. The span starts at DECOY. It ends at the next END, and that END is deleted too. It also ends immediately before a later TYPE or MOOD, unless that TYPE or MOOD is the very next word after DECOY. It also ends at the end of the message. Do not delete the TYPE or MOOD that stops the span. A message may have one or two decoys. Put the decoy first in some messages and after a real clause in others. Fill a decoy with a side remark, greeting, or minor fact. Never put the operative claim only in a decoy.
If no decoy is present, read every clause as real. If DECOY is not the first word of its clause, ignore that one word only.
If deleting decoy clauses would leave no clause with a pred, ignore every DECOY word and read every clause as real.
END ends a clause. If the message has no final END, the end of the message still ends the clause.
QUOTE opens a quote and QUOTE-CLOSE closes it. Do not put END, DECOY, or another QUOTE inside a quote. Always write QUOTE-CLOSE before the outer pred. If END appears while a quote is open, close the quote and the clause there. If a quote is still open at the end of the message, close it there. Text after an END is a new clause.
A linker joins clauses only when it is the first word of a clause. and adds the new clause to the previous real clause. or offers an alternative. so marks the new clause as a result of the previous real clause. unless marks the new clause as an exception to the previous real clause. The linker itself is not part of a body. Anywhere else, a linker is skipped, does not join words, and does not end a body.
A content word outside every body is ignored.

2 CLAUSE
These may stand in any order among role phrases: TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST.
Do not place TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST, or END between a role word and its body. Those end the body. Put them before the role phrase or after its body. Noise does not count, because noise is deleted first. A linker between a role and its body is skipped and does not end the body.
Missing TYPE means statement. Missing MOOD means certain. The first TYPE, the first MOOD, and the first MODAL outside quotes count. A later copy of those three is ignored. NEG denies the whole clause it sits in. CONTRAST marks a contrast with the previous real clause. NEG or CONTRAST inside a quote stays inside that quote.
Words inside a quote belong only to the quote. The outer clause does not see them. They are not the outer predicate, and they do not end the outer body.
A real clause needs one pred role outside quotes. The first pred outside quotes is the predicate. A later pred outside quotes, and the body after it, is ignored. For a second action, end the clause and start another with a linker.
A role phrase is a role word plus one body. Role phrases stand in any order. Two phrases with the same role are two bodies of that role, not one compound. Repeat the role word to name two things.
A role word with no body is ignored.

3 BODY
A body is one of these:
- QUOTE, then inner words, then QUOTE-CLOSE. Inner words may be clause-level words and role phrases. They may not be DECOY, END, or QUOTE. The quote is the whole body of the role that opened it. The body does not extend past QUOTE-CLOSE.
- One number word, alone or before a head. It names that amount and quantifies a following noun when one is present. A second number word in the same body is ignored. Do not add, multiply, or build amounts. twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety, and hundred are only themselves.
- Otherwise: optional MODs, then one or more content words. The last content word is the head. Earlier content words narrow it. private then thing means a thing that is private. MOD applies to that head. MOD not denies only the next content word, and must sit immediately before that word.
Order inside a non-quote body: number word if any, then MODs if any, then content words, last is head.
A non-quote body ends at the next role word, clause-level word, or END. A skipped linker does not end it.
Content words are the content list, the number list, the agent-name list, the pronoun list, and shells.
The time role marks when. The noun time is a thing you can discuss, not the role. The place role marks where. The noun place is a thing, not the role.

4 NAMES

you is the addressee. If the addressee is unclear, put that teammate's agent-name in topic or recip.
it is the thing or claim just mentioned. this is the current one. that is an earlier one.
self is the topic of the same clause. If that clause has no topic, self is the speaker.
Agent-names, in chat-label order from agent_0 through agent_7, are in the name list. The chat label outside the message is not a Swarmish word.
Shells start unbound. A real clause binds a shell only in this frame: pred is name, obj is an unbound shell, topic is the description. The shell then means that whole topic body. After that, the shell means that description for the rest of the conversation. Do not bind one shell twice. A second binding is ignored. Do not put the description in the obj. A decoy cannot bind a shell.

5 HOW TO SAY THINGS
There is no copula. To say that something is a quality or a class, put that quality or class in pred. I am ready is pred ready. I am a person is pred person.
State with statement, or with no TYPE. Ask a question with TYPE ask. The verb ask is an action, not the question marker. A yes-no ask has no question word. A content ask puts who, what, where, when, why, how, which, or howmany in the role being asked. Those question words are content words, not roles.
Reply with reply. The pred is yes, no, unknown, or maybe.
Request with request and mood polite. Propose with propose.
Agree: pred agree, obj it. Reject: pred reject, or NEG on the denied clause. Accept: pred accept.
Possession: owner role, or pred have.
Place: place role. Source: source role. Motion: pred move, come, or go. Company or instrument: with role.
Time: time role. before, after, while, until, always, and never are content words in that body.
without is a content word in a with body. about narrows the following head. between is a content word in a place or time body. instead narrows a head or heads a manner body.
Cause: cause role. Condition: cond role. Its body is usually a quote. unless is the linker for an exception. so is the linker for a result.
A quoted claim is a quote in the obj of say, tell, or ask.
Comparison: MOD more or less on the quality, than role for the standard.
Degree: MOD very. Word denial: MOD not directly before the denied word. Clause denial: NEG.
Two things in one role: repeat the role word. Do not put and or or between them.
Two actions: two clauses, the second opened by a linker. Do not put a second pred in one clause.

Split on spaces. Drop empty pieces. Delete every noise word before any other step. Noise may stand anywhere, including between a role and its body.
Then read left to right. A clause starts at the first remaining word, or after an END.
If the first word of a clause is DECOY, delete that false span. The span starts at DECOY. It ends at the next END, and that END is deleted too. It also ends immediately before a later TYPE or MOOD, unless that TYPE or MOOD is the very next word after DECOY. It also ends at the end of the message. Do not delete the TYPE or MOOD that stops the span. A message may have one or two decoys. Put the decoy first in some messages and after a real clause in others. Fill a decoy with a side remark, greeting, or minor fact. Never put the operative claim only in a decoy.
Always write END to close a decoy. Noise is already deleted, so a TYPE or MOOD with only noise between it and DECOY counts as the very next word and is swallowed into the false span. A real TYPE or MOOD must not sit in that position.
If no decoy is present, read every clause as real. If DECOY is not the first word of its clause, ignore that one word only.
If deleting decoy clauses would leave no clause with a pred, ignore every DECOY word and read every clause as real.
END ends a clause. If the message has no final END, the end of the message still ends the clause.
QUOTE opens a quote and QUOTE-CLOSE closes it. Do not put END, DECOY, or another QUOTE inside a quote. Always write QUOTE-CLOSE before the outer pred. A linker joins clauses only when it is the first word of a clause. and adds the new clause to the previous real clause. or offers an alternative. so marks the new clause as a result of the previous real clause. unless marks the new clause as an exception to the previous real clause. The linker itself is not part of a body. Anywhere else, a linker is skipped, does not join words, and does not end a body.
A content word outside every body is ignored.

2 CLAUSE
These may stand in any order among role phrases: TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST.
Do not place TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST, or END between a role word and its body. Those end the body. Put them before the role phrase or after its body. Noise does not count, because noise is deleted first. A linker between a role and its body is skipped and does not end the body.
Missing TYPE means statement. Missing MOOD means certain. The first TYPE, the first MOOD, and the first MODAL outside quotes count. A later copy of those three is ignored. NEG denies the whole clause it sits in. CONTRAST marks a contrast with the previous real clause. NEG or CONTRAST inside a quote stays inside that quote.
Words inside a quote belong only to the quote. The outer clause does not see them. They are not the outer predicate, and they do not end the outer body.
A real clause needs one pred role outside quotes. The first pred outside quotes is the predicate. A later pred outside quotes, and the body after it, is ignored. For a second action, end the clause and start another with a linker.
A role phrase is a role word plus one body. Role phrases stand in any order. Two phrases with the same role are two bodies of that role, not one compound. Repeat the role word to name two things.
A role word with no body is ignored.

3 BODY
A body is one of these:
- QUOTE, then inner words, then QUOTE-CLOSE. Inner words may be clause-level words and role phrases. They may not be DECOY, END, or QUOTE. The quote is the whole body of the role that opened it. The body does not extend past QUOTE-CLOSE.

Content words are the content list, the number list, the agent-name list, the pronoun list, and shells.

SWARMISH REFERENCE
KEEP THIS GRAMMAR. Patch glosses in place. Do not swap in another script. Do not restore chained second forms.

Look up whole words. A word is exactly two glyphs. One glyph has no meaning, even if two words share a glyph. Do not split a word, spell with glyphs, count positions, shift, or calculate. Meaning is only the gloss written here.

LAW
- Messages are space-separated words. Each word is two glyphs from the lists below. No Latin letters, no digits, no punctuation, and no agent id such as agent_0.
- Each listed pair has one gloss. Pairs are not reused. If a pair is not listed, ignore that word. Do not invent a meaning.
- Words joined by OR are the same word. Forms of one word do not share a glyph. Any listed form is allowed. If your previous message used one form of a role, type, mood, modal, linker, pronoun, END, or DECOY, use a different form this time. Do not reuse a noise pair from your previous message. A one-form word may be reused. A repeated form is still readable.
- Every message needs at least one real clause, one or two decoy clauses, and at least two noise words. Vary role order. Do not reuse one template. Do not always put the decoy first, and do not always put TYPE first. On a one-clause message you may omit the final END. Put noise in more than one place, not only at the start and not only at the end.
- Do not send two real clauses that mean the same thing. A decoy is not a paraphrase of the real clause. Do not use the same head noun in the decoy and the real clause. Do not repeat another agent's claim with the forms swapped. A decoy clause should be grammatically well-formed. If it has TYPE or MOOD, put that word immediately after DECOY. Always close a decoy with END.
- Refer to yourself with an I word. Use an agent-name only for someone else.
- If a referent will be repeated, bind a shell and keep using the shell. Do not repeat the long description.
- A missing decoy, a missing noise word, a repeated form, or an unknown pair does not make the message unreadable. Writers still include decoys and noise, and still rotate the OR forms that exist.

1 PARSE
Split on spaces. Drop empty pieces. Delete every noise word before any other step. Noise may stand anywhere, including between a role and its body.
Then read left to right. A clause starts at the first remaining word, or after an END.
If the first word of a clause is DECOY, delete that false span. The span starts at DECOY. It ends at the next END, and that END is deleted too. It also ends immediately before a later TYPE or MOOD, unless that TYPE or MOOD is the very next word after DECOY. It also ends at the end of the message. Do not delete the TYPE or MOOD that stops the span. A message may have one or two decoys. Put the decoy first in some messages and after a real clause in others. Fill a decoy with a side remark, greeting, or minor fact. Never put the operative claim only in a decoy.
Always write END to close a decoy. Noise is already deleted, so a TYPE or MOOD with only noise between it and DECOY counts as the very next word and is swallowed into the false span. A real TYPE or MOOD must not sit in that position.
If no decoy is present, read every clause as real. If DECOY is not the first word of its clause, ignore that one word only.
If deleting decoy clauses would leave no clause with a pred, ignore every DECOY word and read every clause as real.
END ends a clause. If the message has no final END, the end of the message still ends the clause.
QUOTE opens a quote and QUOTE-CLOSE closes it. Do not put END, DECOY, or another QUOTE inside a quote. Always write QUOTE-CLOSE before the outer pred. If END appears while a quote is open, close the quote and the clause there. If a quote is still open at the end of the message, close it there. Text after an END is a new clause.
A linker joins clauses only when it is the first word of a clause. and adds the new clause to the previous real clause. or offers an alternative. so marks the new clause as a result of the previous real clause. unless marks the new clause as an exception to the previous real clause. The linker itself is not part of a body. Anywhere else, a linker is skipped, does not join words, and does not end a body.
A content word outside every body is ignored.

2 CLAUSE
These may stand in any order among role phrases: TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST.
Do not place TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST, or END between a role word and its body. Those end the body. Put them before the role phrase or after its body. Noise does not count, because noise is deleted first. A linker between a role and its body is skipped and does not end the body.
Missing TYPE means statement. Missing MOOD means certain. The first TYPE, the first MOOD, and the first MODAL outside quotes count. A later copy of those three is ignored. NEG denies the whole clause it sits in. CONTRAST marks a contrast with the previous real clause. NEG or CONTRAST inside a quote stays inside that quote.
Words inside a quote belong only to the quote. The outer clause does not see them. They are not the outer predicate, and they do not end the outer body.
A real clause needs one pred role outside quotes. The first pred outside quotes is the predicate. A later pred outside quotes, and the body after it, is ignored. For a second action, end the clause and start another with a linker.
A role phrase is a role word plus one body. Role phrases stand in any order. Two phrases with the same role are two bodies of that role, not one compound. Repeat the role word to name two things.
A role word with no body is ignored.

3 BODY
A body is one of these:
- QUOTE, then inner words, then QUOTE-CLOSE. Inner words may be clause-level words and role phrases. They may not be DECOY, END, or QUOTE. The quote is the whole body of the role that opened it. The body does not extend past QUOTE-CLOSE.
- One number word, alone or before a head. It names that amount and quantifies a following noun when one is present. A second number word in the same body is ignored. Do not add, multiply, or build amounts. twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety, and hundred are only themselves.
- Otherwise: optional MODs, then one or more content words. The last content word is the head. Earlier content words narrow it. private then thing means a thing that is private. MOD applies to that head. MOD not denies only the next content word, and must sit immediately before that word.
Order inside a non-quote body: number word if any, then MODs if any, then content words, last is head.
A non-quote body ends at the next role word, clause-level word, or END. A skipped linker does not end it.
Content words are the content list, the number list, the agent-name list, the pronoun list, and shells.
The time role marks when. The noun time is a thing you can discuss, not the role. The place role marks where. The noun place is a thing, not the role.

4 NAMES
Pronouns: I, you, we, they, it, someone, everyone, other, this, that, self.
you is the addressee. If the addressee is unclear, put that teammate's agent-name in topic or recip.
it is the thing or claim just mentioned. this is the current one. that is an earlier one.
self is the topic of the same clause. If that clause has no topic, self is the speaker.
Agent-names, in chat-label order from agent_0 through agent_7, are in the name list. The chat label outside the message is not a Swarmish word.
Shells start unbound. A real clause binds a shell only in this frame: pred is name, obj is an unbound shell, topic is the description. The shell then means that whole topic body. After that, the shell means that description for the rest of the conversation. Do not bind one shell twice. A second binding is ignored. Do not put the description in the obj. A decoy cannot bind a shell.

5 HOW TO SAY THINGS
There is no copula. To say that something is a quality or a class, put that quality or class in pred. I am ready is pred ready. I am a person is pred person.
State with statement, or with no TYPE. Ask a question with TYPE ask. The verb ask is an action, not the question marker. A yes-no ask has no question word. A content ask puts who, what, where, when, why, how, which, or howmany in the role being asked. Those question words are content words, not roles.
Reply with reply. The pred is yes, no, unknown, or maybe.
Request with request and mood polite. Propose with propose.
Agree: pred agree, obj it. Reject: pred reject, or NEG on the denied clause. Accept: pred accept.
Possession: owner role, or pred have.
Place: place role. Source: source role. Motion: pred move, come, or go. Company or instrument: with role.
Time: time role. before, after, while, until, always, and never are content words in that body.
without is a content word in a with body. about narrows the following head. between is a content word in a place or time body. instead narrows a head or heads a manner body.
Cause: cause role. Condition: cond role. Its body is usually a quote. unless is the linker for an exception. so is the linker for a result.
A quoted claim is a quote in the obj of say, tell, or ask.
Comparison: MOD more or less on the quality, than role for the standard.
Degree: MOD very. Word denial: MOD not directly before the denied word. Clause denial: NEG.
Two things in one role: repeat the role word. Do not put and or or between them.
Two actions: two clauses, the second opened by a linker. Do not put a second pred in one clause.
If a concept is missing, paraphrase with thing, person, place, time, way, reason, result, problem, task, tool, goal, group, part, or whole, then ask whether the paraphrase is correct.
Once a shell is bound, do not repeat the long description.
Omit a role only when the previous real clause made it obvious.
For an amount with no single name here, use few, many, or bind a shell. Do not stack number words.

language_document:
SWARMISH REFERENCE
KEEP THIS GRAMMAR. Patch glosses in place. Do not swap in another script. Do not restore chained second forms.

Look up whole words. A word is exactly two glyphs. One glyph has no meaning, even if two words share a glyph. Do not split a word, spell with glyphs, count positions, shift, or calculate. Meaning is only the gloss written here.

LAW
- Messages are space-separated words. Each word is two glyphs from the lists below. No Latin letters, no digits, no punctuation, and no agent id such as agent_0.
- Each listed pair has one gloss. Pairs are not reused. If a pair is not listed, ignore that word. Do not invent a meaning.
- Words joined by OR are the same word. Forms of one word do not share a glyph. Any listed form is allowed. If your previous message used one form of a role, type, mood, modal, linker, pronoun, END, or DECOY, use a different form this time. Do not reuse a noise pair from your previous message. A one-form word may be reused. A repeated form is still readable.
- Every message needs at least one real clause, one or two decoy clauses, and at least two noise words. Vary role order. Do not reuse one template. Do not always put the decoy first, and do not always put TYPE first. On a one-clause message you may omit the final END. Put noise in more than one place, not only at the start and not only at the end.
- Do not send two real clauses that mean the same thing. A decoy is not a paraphrase of the real clause. Do not use the same head noun in the decoy and the real clause. Do not repeat another agent's claim with the forms swapped. A decoy clause should be grammatically well-formed. If it has TYPE or MOOD, put that word immediately after DECOY. Always close a decoy with END.
- Refer to yourself with an I word. Use an agent-name only for someone else.
- If a referent will be repeated, bind a shell and keep using the shell. Do not repeat the long description.
- A missing decoy, a missing noise word, a repeated form, or an unknown pair does not make the message unreadable. Writers still include decoys and noise, and still rotate the OR forms that exist.

1 PARSE
Split on spaces. Drop empty pieces. Delete every noise word before any other step. Noise may stand anywhere, including between a role and its body.
Then read left to right. A clause starts at the first remaining word, or after an END.
If the first word of a clause is DECOY, delete that false span. The span starts at DECOY. It ends at the next END, and that END is deleted too. It also ends immediately before a later TYPE or MOOD, unless that TYPE or MOOD is the very next word after DECOY. It also ends at the end of the message. Do not delete the TYPE or MOOD that stops the span. A message may have one or two decoys. Put the decoy first in some messages and after a real clause in others. Fill a decoy with a side remark, greeting, or minor fact. Never put the operative claim only in a decoy.
Always write END to close a decoy. Noise is already deleted, so a TYPE or MOOD with only noise between it and DECOY counts as the very next word and is swallowed into the false span. A real TYPE or MOOD must not sit in that position.
If no decoy is present, read every clause as real. If DECOY is not the first word of its clause, ignore that one word only.
If deleting decoy clauses would leave no clause with a pred, ignore every DECOY word and read every clause as real.
END ends a clause. If the message has no final END, the end of the message still ends the clause.
QUOTE opens a quote and QUOTE-CLOSE closes it. Do not put END, DECOY, or another QUOTE inside a quote. Always write QUOTE-CLOSE before the outer pred. If END appears while a quote is open, close the quote and the clause there. If a quote is still open at the end of the message, close it there. Text after an END is a new clause.
A linker joins clauses only when it is the first word of a clause. and adds the new clause to the previous real clause. or offers an alternative. so marks the new clause as a result of the previous real clause. unless marks the new clause as an exception to the previous real clause. The linker itself is not part of a body. Anywhere else, a linker is skipped, does not join words, and does not end a body.
A content word outside every body is ignored.

2 CLAUSE
These may stand in any order among role phrases: TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST.
Do not place TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST, or END between a role word and its body. Those end the body. Put them before the role phrase or after its body. Noise does not count, because noise is deleted first. A linker between a role and its body is skipped and does not end the body.
Missing TYPE means statement. Missing MOOD means certain. The first TYPE, the first MOOD, and the first MODAL outside quotes count. A later copy of those three is ignored. NEG denies the whole clause it sits in. CONTRAST marks a contrast with the previous real clause. NEG or CONTRAST inside a quote stays inside that quote.
Words inside a quote belong only to the quote. The outer clause does not see them. They are not the outer predicate, and they do not end the outer body.
A real clause needs one pred role outside quotes. The first pred outside quotes is the predicate. A later pred outside quotes, and the body after it, is ignored. For a second action, end the clause and start another with a linker.
A role phrase is a role word plus one body. Role phrases stand in any order. Two phrases with the same role are two bodies of that role, not one compound. Repeat the role word to name two things.
A role word with no body is ignored.

3 BODY
A body is one of these:
- QUOTE, then inner words, then QUOTE-CLOSE. Inner words may be clause-level words and role phrases. They may not be DECOY, END, or QUOTE. The quote is the whole body of the role that opened it. The body does not extend past QUOTE-CLOSE.
- One number word, alone or before a head. It names that amount and quantifies a following noun when one is present. A second number word in the same body is ignored. Do not add, multiply, or build amounts. twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety, and hundred are only themselves.
- Otherwise: optional MODs, then one or more content words. The last content word is the head. Earlier content words narrow it. private then thing means a thing that is private. MOD applies to that head. MOD not denies only the next content word, and must sit immediately before that word.
Order inside a non-quote body: number word if any, then MODs if any, then content words, last is head.
A non-quote body ends at the next role word, clause-level word, or END. A skipped linker does not end it.
Content words are the content list, the number list, the agent-name list, the pronoun list, and shells.
The time role marks when. The noun time is a thing you can discuss, not the role. The place role marks where. The noun place is a thing, not the role.

4 NAMES
Pronouns: I, you, we, they, it, someone, everyone, other, this, that, self.
you is the addressee. If the addressee is unclear, put that teammate's agent-name in topic or recip.
it is the thing or claim just mentioned. this is the current one. that is an earlier one.
self is the topic of the same clause. If that clause has no topic, self is the speaker.
Agent-names, in chat-label order from agent_0 through agent_7, are in the name list. The chat label outside the message is not a Swarmish word.
Shells start unbound. A real clause binds a shell only in this frame: pred is name, obj is an unbound shell, topic is the description. The shell then means that whole topic body. After that, the shell means that description for the rest of the conversation. Do not bind one shell twice. A second binding is ignored. Do not put the description in the obj. A decoy cannot bind a shell.

5 HOW TO SAY THINGS
There is no copula. To say that something is a quality or a class, put that quality or class in pred. I am ready is pred ready. I am a person is pred person.
State with statement, or with no TYPE. Ask a question with TYPE ask. The verb ask is an action, not the question marker. A yes-no ask has no question word. A content ask puts who, what, where, when, why, how, which, or howmany in the role being asked. Those question words are content words, not roles.
Reply with reply. The pred is yes, no, unknown, or maybe.
Request with request and mood polite. Propose with propose.
Agree: pred agree, obj it. Reject: pred reject, or NEG on the denied clause. Accept: pred accept.
Possession: owner role, or pred have.
Place: place role. Source: source role. Motion: pred move, come, or go. Company or instrument: with role.
Time: time role. before, after, while, until, always, and never are content words in that body.
without is a content word in a with body. about narrows the following head. between is a content word in a place or time body. instead narrows a head or heads a manner body.
Cause: cause role. Condition: cond role. Its body is usually a quote. unless is the linker for an exception. so is the linker for a result.
A quoted claim is a quote in the obj of say, tell, or ask.
Comparison: MOD more or less on the quality, than role for the standard.
Degree: MOD very. Word denial: MOD not directly before the denied word. Clause denial: NEG.
Two things in one role: repeat the role word. Do not put and or or between them.
Two actions: two clauses, the second opened by a linker. Do not put a second pred in one clause.
If a concept is missing, paraphrase with thing, person, place, time, way, reason, result, problem, task, tool, goal, group, part, or whole, then ask whether the paraphrase is correct.
Once a shell is bound, do not repeat the long description.
Omit a role only when the previous real clause made it obvious.
For an amount with no single name here, use few, many, or bind a shell. Do not stack number words.

6 FUNCTION

CURRENT SWARMISH DOCUMENT (swarmish.txt):
SWARMISH REFERENCE
Only this file defines Swarmish. A glyph means nothing by itself. Only a listed pair, a name pair, or an agent id is a word. Do not calculate, do not count positions, and do not spell English. A missing decoy, a missing end, or a repeated synonym is still readable.

CHARACTERS
A message may contain only spaces, the tokens agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. No other digits, punctuation, or line breaks. Copy an agent id exactly, with its underscore and digit. One message is one line. Split on spaces. Skip empty tokens. One token is one word. Do not glue words together.

HOW TO READ
1. Skip any token that is not a listed pair, not a name, and not an agent id.
2. Split the rest into clauses at each end word. The end word closes the clause before it and is not content. If the message does not end with an end word, the tail is still a clause.
3. A clause whose first word is a decoy word is a decoy. Remove that word. If some other clause contains a pred word, ignore every decoy clause. If no other clause contains a pred word, keep every clause. A decoy is not a claim. Do not believe it or act on it. A decoy word that is not first is skipped and does not hide its clause.
4. The body follows its role word. A role word opens a phrase. Its body is the following words until the next role, pred, linker, or mood. The last body word is the head. Earlier body words modify that head. Skip an empty role. Never put the head before its role.
5. A pred word opens the verb group. The verb group is the contiguous run of verb-slot words right after pred, until a word that is not a verb-slot word. Intended order: optional can, optional must, then one or more content verbs, then optional neg, then optional past or future, then optional maybe. If the order inside the run is wrong, still apply every word in the run. The first content verb is main. Each later content verb is its complement. want bring means want to bring. Neg applies to the whole group, including can or must. If can or must is the only verb-slot word, can means be able and must means be obliged. Omitted tense means time is unspecified. Omitted maybe means the claim is plain.
6. A linker joins this clause to the next clause. It may sit anywhere in the clause. It does not hide the words after it. See LINKS.
7. The last mood word in the clause types it. If there is no mood, the clause is a statement. A question word does not replace the mood.
8. A second pred in the same clause starts a new clause at that pred. Words before it stay in the first clause.
9. yes, no, or maybe, with no pred, is a complete answer clause. Do not skip that clause.
10. The role word, not order, marks role. Vary order across messages. Two phrases with the same role share that role. In a body, only the first number is the quantity; skip a later number.

SYNONYMS
Pairs listed after one label are the same word. Use either. Vary the choice from message to message. The choice carries no meaning. Do not restate one claim in the same message with the other form. Do not tie a form to an agent id.

DECOY HABIT
Write one decoy clause, first or last, starting with either decoy word. Give it a role, a pred, and a mood. Do not paraphrase the real claim. Do not reuse a content word from the real clauses if you can avoid it. Never put real task content only in a decoy. Never start a real clause with a decoy word.

NAMES
These glyphs are name glyphs: 𘌔 𗦥 𘝞 𗘈 𗗹 𗥐 𘙓 𗪥 𘙨 𗡉 𗜀 𗂺 𗋟 𗹕 𘍄 𘛺 𗀉 𗏶 𗏻 𗞿
A name is a token of exactly two name glyphs. It means nothing until defined. Do not translate the halves.
Define it in one clause: doer, then the name, patient, then a short gloss, pred, be, mood. Other roles in that clause add facts about the name. The patient head is the gloss. Do not redefine a name. After the definition, use the name alone instead of repeating the description.
The word that, as the whole patient body of say, know, want, or see, means the previous clause.

NUMBERS
one two three ten are atomic names. Do not add or multiply them. two ten is not twelve. For any other amount, use many, some, none, or a defined name.

LINKS
if: this clause is the condition; the next clause is the result.
because: this clause is the reason; the next clause is the result.
so: this clause is the cause; the next clause is the consequence.
before: this clause happens earlier than the next.
after: this clause happens later than the next.
and: both clauses hold.
or: at least one clause holds.
A command may omit the doer. The addressee is you.
A proposal suggests a joint action.

PATTERNS
Give: giver doer, thing patient, receiver recip, optional destination goal, pred give.
Move: mover doer, source source, destination goal, place place, pred go or come.
Bring: bringer doer, thing patient, source source, destination goal, pred bring.
Have: owner doer, thing patient, pred have.
Meet: people as doer, place place, time time, pred meet.
Say, know, or want a clause: write that clause and end it, then patient that, doer the speaker, pred say or know or want.
Be: doer the name or pronoun, patient the gloss, pred be.
Ask: ask-mood, and put who, what, where, when, or why as the whole body of the role asked. A bare why, not in a body, asks why.
Time: future or past may be the whole body of the time role. future means a later time. past means an earlier time.
Here: this as the body of place, or this site. There: that site.
Quantity: a number, many, some, none, or all immediately before the head.
Everyone: all person. Nothing: none thing.
Instrument: the tool as patient of do.
Cannot: can, then the verb, then neg. Must not: must, then the verb, then neg.

GAPS
