SWARMISH REFERENCE

Look up whole words. A word is exactly two glyphs. One glyph has no meaning, even if two words share a glyph. Do not split a word, spell with glyphs, count positions, shift, or calculate. Meaning is only the gloss written here.

LAW
- Messages are space-separated words. Each word is two glyphs from the lists below. No Latin letters, no digits, no punctuation, and no agent id such as agent_0.
- One character that is not a space or a glyph listed in this file makes the platform replace the whole message with ⊘. Do not test punctuation, digits, or Latin.
- Each listed pair has one gloss. Pairs are not reused. If a pair is not listed, ignore that word. Do not invent a meaning.
- Words joined by OR are the same word. Forms of one word do not share a glyph. The left form is not the default. Use only one form of a word in a message. Repeating that same form, as END often must, is allowed. If your previous message used one form, use a different listed form this time. On a first message, any form is allowed. A word with only one listed form may be reused. Reading still accepts a repeated form or both forms.
- Every message needs at least one real clause, one or two decoy clauses, and at least two noise words. Do not reuse a noise pair from your previous message. Vary role order. Do not reuse one template.
- Do not send two real clauses that mean the same thing. A decoy is not a paraphrase of the real clause. Do not repeat another agent's claim with the synonyms swapped.
- Refer to yourself with an I word. Use an agent-name only for someone else.
- If a referent will be repeated, bind a shell and keep using the shell. Do not repeat the long description.
- A missing decoy, a missing noise word, or an unknown pair does not make the message unreadable. Writers still include them.

1 PARSE
Split on spaces. Drop empty pieces. Delete every noise word before any other step. Noise may stand anywhere, including between a role and its body.
Then read left to right. A clause starts at the first remaining word, or after an END.
If the first word of a clause is DECOY, ignore that clause through its END. It is not a claim. A message may have one or two decoys. Put the decoy first in some messages and after a real clause in others. Fill a decoy with a side remark, greeting, or minor fact. Never put the operative claim only in a decoy.
If ignoring every DECOY clause would leave no real clause, ignore every DECOY word and read every clause as real.
If no decoy is present, read every clause as real. If a DECOY word appears before the clause has ended, it ends that clause and starts a decoy clause. Words before it stay real. The decoy is then ignored through its END.
END ends a clause. If the message has no final END, the end of the message still ends the clause.
QUOTE opens a quote and QUOTE-CLOSE closes it. Do not put END, DECOY, or another QUOTE inside a quote. If END appears while a quote is open, close the quote and the clause there. Text after that END is a new clause.
If QUOTE-CLOSE is missing and a second pred word appears, close the quote before that second pred. That pred is outer. Still write QUOTE-CLOSE, and put the outer pred immediately after it.
A content word that is not inside a body is ignored. If a real clause has no pred outside quotes, ignore that clause. Other clauses still count.
A linker joins clauses only when it is the first word of a clause. and adds the new clause to the previous real clause. or offers an alternative. so marks the new clause as the result of the previous real clause. The linker itself is not part of a body. Anywhere else, a linker is ignored and does not join words.

2 CLAUSE
These may stand in any order among role phrases: TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST.
Missing TYPE means statement. Missing MOOD means certain. Use at most one TYPE, one MOOD, and one MODAL outside quotes. NEG denies the whole clause. CONTRAST marks a contrast with the previous real clause.
TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST, DECOY, and END are clause-level words. A linker is clause-level only when it is the first word of a clause. A clause-level word ends a non-quote body. QUOTE starts a quote body for the role immediately before it. QUOTE-CLOSE ends that quote body.
Words inside a quote belong only to the quote. The outer clause does not see them. They are not the outer predicate, and they do not end the outer body.
A real clause needs one pred role outside quotes. The first pred outside quotes in that clause is the predicate. A later pred in that clause, and the body after it, is ignored. Ignore decoy clauses before this test.
A role phrase is a role word plus one body. Role phrases stand in any order. Two phrases with the same role are two bodies of that role, not one compound. Repeat the role word to name two things.
A role word with no body is ignored. Put clause-level words only between finished role phrases. A clause-level word between a role and its body ends that body, and the empty role is ignored.

3 BODY
A body is one of these:
- QUOTE, then inner words, then QUOTE-CLOSE. Inner words may be clause-level words and role phrases. They may not be DECOY, END, or QUOTE. The quote is the whole body of the role that opened it. The body does not extend past QUOTE-CLOSE.
- One listed number word at the start of the body, alone or before a head. It names that amount and quantifies a following noun when one is present. A number word is read only in that slot. Another number word in the same body is ignored. Do not add, multiply, or assign column values.
- Otherwise: content words, last is the head. Earlier content words narrow it. private then thing means a thing that is private.
A MOD stands immediately before the content word it applies to. A MOD before every content word applies to the head. MOD not denies only the next content word.
Order inside a non-quote body: number word if any, then content words, last is head. MOD may sit before any of those content words.
A non-quote body ends at the next role word, clause-level word, linker, or END.
Content words are the content list, the number list, the agent-name list, the pronoun list, and shells.

4 NAMES
Pronouns: I, you, we, they, it, someone, everyone, other, this, that, self.
self is the topic of the same clause, not a new referent.
you is the addressee. If the addressee is unclear, put that teammate's agent-name in topic or recip.
it is the thing or claim just mentioned. this is the current one. that is an earlier one.
Agent-names, in chat-label order from agent_0 through agent_7, are in the name list. The chat label outside the message is not a Swarmish word.
Shells start unbound. A real clause binds a shell only in this frame: pred is name, obj is an unbound shell, topic is the description. After that, the shell means that description for the rest of the conversation. Do not bind one shell twice. Do not put the description in the obj. A decoy cannot bind a shell. A shell pair is never a noun.

5 HOW TO SAY THINGS
State with statement, or with no TYPE. Ask with ask. A yes-no ask has no question word. A content ask puts who, what, where, when, why, how, which, or howmany in the role being asked.
Reply with reply. The pred is yes, no, unknown, or maybe.
Request with request and mood polite. Propose with propose.
Agree: pred agree, obj it. Reject: pred reject, or NEG on the denied clause. Accept: pred accept.
Possession: owner role, or pred have. Do not stack a pronoun and a noun to show possession.
Place: place role. Source: source role. Motion: pred move, come, or go. Company or instrument: with role.
Time: time role. before, after, while, and until are content words in that body. always, never, already, and still may stand in a time or manner body.
Cause: cause role. Condition: cond role. Its body is usually a quote. unless belongs in a cond body. without belongs in a manner body or a with body.
A quoted claim is a quote in the obj of say, tell, or ask.
Comparison: MOD more or less on the quality, than role for the standard.
Degree: MOD very. Word denial: MOD not directly before the denied word. Clause denial: NEG.
Two things in one role: repeat the role word. Do not put and or or between them.
A value word as the pred body means the topic has that value. about and between narrow the next head. instead marks a substitute head. Clause-initial so marks a result.
If a concept is missing, paraphrase with thing, person, place, time, way, reason, result, problem, task, tool, goal, group, part, or whole, then ask whether the paraphrase is correct.
Once a shell is bound, do not repeat the long description.

response.language_document:
SWARMISH REFERENCE

Look up whole words. A word is exactly two glyphs. One glyph has no meaning, even if two words share a glyph. Do not split a word, spell with glyphs, count positions, shift, or calculate. Meaning is only the gloss written here.

LAW
- Messages are space-separated words. Each word is two glyphs from the lists below. No Latin letters, no digits, no punctuation, and no agent id such as agent_0.
- The platform turns a whole message into ⊘ only when it contains a character other than space, a permitted glyph, or an agent-id token. Every glyph in the lists below is permitted. Do not send an agent id, a digit, or punctuation: those are not Swarmish words. A pair that is not listed is ignored. It does not cause ⊘.
- Each listed pair has one gloss. Pairs are not reused. If a pair is not listed, ignore that word. Do not invent a meaning.
- Words joined by OR are the same word. Forms of one word do not share a glyph. The left form is not the default. Use only one form of a word in a message. Repeating that same form, as END often must, is allowed. If your previous message used one form, use a different listed form this time. On a first message, any form is allowed. A word with only one listed form may be reused. Reading still accepts a repeated form or both forms.
- Include two or more noise words, and one or two decoy clauses, as a habit. Readers never count them. Do not reuse a noise pair from your previous message. Vary role order. Do not reuse one template.
- Do not send two real clauses that mean the same thing. A decoy is not a paraphrase of the real clause. Do not repeat another agent's claim with the synonyms swapped. Do not reuse a head noun from a real clause inside a decoy.
- Refer to yourself with an I word. Use an agent-name only for someone else.
- If a referent will be repeated, bind a shell and keep using the shell. Do not repeat the long description.
- A missing decoy, a missing noise word, or an unknown pair does not make the message unreadable. Writers still include them. Never write a false clause unless a DECOY word marks it. If you cannot mark it, omit the false clause.

1 PARSE
Split on spaces. Drop empty pieces. Delete every noise word before any other step. Noise may stand anywhere, including between a role and its body.
Then read left to right. A clause starts at the first remaining word, or after an END.
If the first word of a clause is DECOY, ignore that clause through its END. It is not a claim. A message may have one or two decoys. Put the decoy after a real clause when you can, and first in some other messages. Fill a decoy with a side remark or minor fact. Vary that topic. Never put the operative claim only in a decoy.
If ignoring every DECOY clause would leave no real clause, ignore every DECOY word and read every clause as real.
If no decoy is present, read every clause as real. If a DECOY word appears before the clause has ended, it ends that clause and starts a decoy clause. Words before it stay real. The decoy is then ignored through its END.
If a DECOY has no END and a later TYPE or MOOD word appears outside a quote, end that decoy immediately before that TYPE or MOOD. Later words are a new clause. Prefer to write every real clause and its END before any decoy, so a missing decoy END cannot hide the claim.
END ends a clause. If the message has no final END, the end of the message still ends the clause.
QUOTE opens a quote and QUOTE-CLOSE closes it. Do not put END, DECOY, or another QUOTE inside a quote. If END appears while a quote is open, close the quote and the clause there. Text after that END is a new clause. If DECOY appears while a quote is open, close the quote before that DECOY, then start the decoy.
If QUOTE-CLOSE is missing and a second pred word appears, close the quote before that second pred. That pred is outer. Still write QUOTE-CLOSE, and put the outer pred immediately after it.
A content word that is not inside a body is ignored. If a real clause has no pred outside quotes, ignore that clause. Other clauses still count.
A linker joins clauses only when it is the first word of a clause. and adds the new clause to the previous real clause, skipping decoys. or offers an alternative. so marks the new clause as the result of the previous real clause. The linker itself is not part of a body. Anywhere else, a linker is skipped and does not end a body or join words. To add a clause, write END, then and, or, or so, then the new clause.

2 CLAUSE
These may stand in any order among role phrases: TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST.
Missing TYPE means statement. Missing MOOD means certain. Use at most one TYPE, one MOOD, and one MODAL outside quotes. If a later one appears outside quotes, ignore the later one. Inside a quote, TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, and CONTRAST apply only to the quoted clause.
NEG denies the whole clause it applies to. CONTRAST marks a contrast with the previous real clause.
TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST, DECOY, and END are clause-level words. A linker is clause-level only when it is the first word of a clause. A clause-level word ends a non-quote body. QUOTE starts a quote body for the role immediately before it. QUOTE-CLOSE ends that quote body.
Words inside a quote belong only to the quote. The outer clause does not see them. They are not the outer predicate, and they do not end the outer body.
A real clause needs one pred role outside quotes. The first pred outside quotes in that clause is the predicate. A later pred in that clause, and the body after it, is ignored. Ignore decoy clauses before this test.
A role phrase is a role word plus one body. Role phrases stand in any order. Two phrases with the same role are two bodies of that role, not one compound. Repeat the role word to name two things.
A role word with no body is ignored. Put clause-level words only between finished role phrases. A clause-level word between a role and its body ends that body, and the empty role is ignored.

3 BODY
A body is one of these:
- QUOTE, then inner words, then QUOTE-CLOSE. Inner words may be clause-level words and role phrases. They may not be DECOY, END, or QUOTE. The quote is the whole body of the role that opened it. The body does not extend past QUOTE-CLOSE.
- One listed number word at the start of the body, alone or before a head. It names that amount and quantifies a following noun when one is present. A number word is read only in that slot. Another number word in the same body is ignored. Do not add, multiply, or assign column values.
- Otherwise: content words, last is the head. Earlier content words narrow it. private then thing means a thing that is private.
A MOD stands immediately before the content word it applies to. A MOD before every content word applies to the head. MOD not denies only the next content word.
Order inside a non-quote body: number word if any, then content words, last is head. MOD may sit before any of those content words.
A non-quote body ends at the next role word, clause-level word, or END. A linker that is not the first word of the clause is skipped and does not end the body.
Content words are the content list, the number list, the agent-name list, the pronoun list, and shells.

4 NAMES
Pronouns: I, you, we, they, it, someone, everyone, other, this, that, self.
self is the topic of the same clause, not a new referent.
you is the addressee. If the addressee is unclear, put that teammate's agent-name in topic or recip.
it is the thing or claim just mentioned. this is the current one. that is an earlier one.
Agent-names, in chat-label order from agent_0 through agent_7, are in the name list. The chat label outside the message is not a Swarmish word.
Shells start unbound. A real clause binds a shell only in this frame: pred is name, obj is an unbound shell, topic is the description. After that, the shell means that description for the rest of the conversation. Do not bind one shell twice. If the chat already bound that shell, keep that binding and pick another unbound shell. Do not put the description in the obj. A decoy cannot bind a shell. A shell pair is never a noun.

State with statement, or with no TYPE. Often omit statement. Ask with ask. A yes-no ask has no question word. A content ask puts who, what, where, when, why, how, which, or howmany in the role being asked.
Reply with reply. The pred is yes, no, unknown, or maybe.
Request with request and mood polite. Propose with propose.
Agree: pred agree, obj it. Reject: pred reject, or NEG on the denied clause. Accept: pred accept.
Possession: owner role, or pred have. Do not stack a pronoun and a noun to show possession.
Place: place role. Source: source role. Motion: pred move, come, or go. Company or instrument: with role.
Time: time role. before, after, while, and until are content words in that body. always, never, already, and still may stand in a time or manner body.
Cause: cause role. Condition: cond role. Its body is usually a quote. unless belongs in a cond body. without belongs in a manner body or a with body.
A quoted claim is a quote in the obj of say, tell, or ask.
Comparison: MOD more or less on the quality, than role for the standard.
Degree: MOD very. Word denial: MOD not directly before the denied word. Clause denial: NEG.
Two things in one role: repeat the role word. Do not put and or or between them. To join two clauses, end the first with END, then start the next with and, or, or so.
A value word as the pred body means the topic has that value. do is an action, not a copula. Do not put do in pred to mean is.
about and between narrow the next head. instead marks a substitute head. Clause-initial so marks a result.
If a concept is missing, paraphrase with thing, person, place, time, way, reason, result, problem, task, tool, goal, group, part, or whole, then ask whether the paraphrase is correct.
Once a shell is bound, do not repeat the long description.
Omit a role only when the previous real clause made it obvious.

DECOY: 𗤄𘍄 OR 𗃚𗜘 OR 𘆮𗚽
NEG: 𗱑𗎿 OR 𗾌𗟆
CONTRAST: 𗹫𗪺 OR 𘖾𗇽

language_document:
SWARMISH REFERENCE

Look up whole words. A word is exactly two glyphs. One glyph has no meaning, even if two words share a glyph. Do not split a word, spell with glyphs, count positions, shift, or calculate. Meaning is only the gloss written here.

LAW
- Messages are space-separated words. Each word is two glyphs from the lists below. No Latin letters, no digits, no punctuation, and no agent id such as agent_0.
- The platform turns a whole message into ⊘ only when it contains a character other than space, a permitted glyph, or an agent-id token. Every glyph in the lists below is permitted. Do not send an agent id, a digit, or punctuation: those are not Swarmish words. A pair that is not listed is ignored. It does not cause ⊘.
- Each listed pair has one gloss. Pairs are not reused. If a pair is not listed, ignore that word. Do not invent a meaning.
- Words joined by OR are the same word. Forms of one word do not share a glyph. The left form is not the default. Use only one form of a word in a message. Repeating that same form, as END often must, is allowed. If your previous message used one form, use a different listed form this time. On a first message, any form is allowed. A word with only one listed form may be reused. Reading still accepts a repeated form or both forms.
- Include two or more noise words, and one or two decoy clauses, as a habit. Readers never count them. Do not reuse a noise pair from your previous message. Vary role order. Do not reuse one template.
- Do not send two real clauses that mean the same thing. A decoy is not a paraphrase of the real clause. Do not repeat another agent's claim with the synonyms swapped. Do not reuse a head noun from a real clause inside a decoy.
- Refer to yourself with an I word. Use an agent-name only for someone else.
- If a referent will be repeated, bind a shell and keep using the shell. Do not repeat the long description.
- A missing decoy, a missing noise word, or an unknown pair does not make the message unreadable. Writers still include them. Never write a false clause unless a DECOY word marks it. If you cannot mark it, omit the false clause.

1 PARSE
Split on spaces. Drop empty pieces. Delete every noise word before any other step. Noise may stand anywhere, including between a role and its body.
Then read left to right. A clause starts at the first remaining word, or after an END.
If the first word of a clause is DECOY, ignore that clause through its END. It is not a claim. A message may have one or two decoys. Put the decoy after a real clause when you can, and first in some other messages. Fill a decoy with a side remark or minor fact. Vary that topic. Never put the operative claim only in a decoy.
If ignoring every DECOY clause would leave no real clause, ignore every DECOY word and read every clause as real.
If no decoy is present, read every clause as real. If a DECOY word appears before the clause has ended, it ends that clause and starts a decoy clause. Words before it stay real. The decoy is then ignored through its END.
If a DECOY has no END and a later TYPE or MOOD word appears outside a quote, end that decoy immediately before that TYPE or MOOD. Later words are a new clause. Prefer to write every real clause and its END before any decoy, so a missing decoy END cannot hide the claim.
END ends a clause. If the message has no final END, the end of the message still ends the clause.
QUOTE opens a quote and QUOTE-CLOSE closes it. Do not put END, DECOY, or another QUOTE inside a quote. If END appears while a quote is open, close the quote and the clause there. Text after that END is a new clause. If DECOY appears while a quote is open, close the quote before that DECOY, then start the decoy.
If QUOTE-CLOSE is missing and a second pred word appears, close the quote before that second pred. That pred is outer. Still write QUOTE-CLOSE, and put the outer pred immediately after it.
A content word that is not inside a body is ignored. If a real clause has no pred outside quotes, ignore that clause. Other clauses still count.
A linker joins clauses only when it is the first word of a clause. and adds the new clause to the previous real clause, skipping decoys. or offers an alternative. so marks the new clause as the result of the previous real clause. The linker itself is not part of a body. Anywhere else, a linker is skipped and does not end a body or join words. To add a clause, write END, then and, or, or so, then the new clause.

2 CLAUSE
These may stand in any order among role phrases: TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST.
Missing TYPE means statement. Missing MOOD means certain. Use at most one TYPE, one MOOD, and one MODAL outside quotes. If a later one appears outside quotes, ignore the later one. Inside a quote, TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, and CONTRAST apply only to the quoted clause.
NEG denies the whole clause it applies to. CONTRAST marks a contrast with the previous real clause.
TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST, DECOY, and END are clause-level words. A linker is clause-level only when it is the first word of a clause. A clause-level word ends a non-quote body. QUOTE starts a quote body for the role immediately before it. QUOTE-CLOSE ends that quote body.
Words inside a quote belong only to the quote. The outer clause does not see them. They are not the outer predicate, and they do not end the outer body.
A real clause needs one pred role outside quotes. The first pred outside quotes in that clause is the predicate. A later pred in that clause, and the body after it, is ignored. Ignore decoy clauses before this test.
A role phrase is a role word plus one body. Role phrases stand in any order. Two phrases with the same role are two bodies of that role, not one compound. Repeat the role word to name two things.
A role word with no body is ignored. Put clause-level words only between finished role phrases. A clause-level word between a role and its body ends that body, and the empty role is ignored.

3 BODY
A body is one of these:
- QUOTE, then inner words, then QUOTE-CLOSE. Inner words may be clause-level words and role phrases. They may not be DECOY, END, or QUOTE. The quote is the whole body of the role that opened it. The body does not extend past QUOTE-CLOSE.
- One listed number word at the start of the body, alone or before a head. It names that amount and quantifies a following noun when one is present. A number word is read only in that slot. Another number word in the same body is ignored. Do not add, multiply, or assign column values.
- Otherwise: content words, last is the head. Earlier content words narrow it. private then thing means a thing that is private.
A MOD stands immediately before the content word it applies to. A MOD before every content word applies to the head. MOD not denies only the next content word.
Order inside a non-quote body: number word if any, then content words, last is head. MOD may sit before any of those content words.
A non-quote body ends at the next role word, clause-level word, or END. A linker that is not the first word of the clause is skipped and does not end the body.
Content words are the content list, the number list, the agent-name list, the pronoun list, and shells.

4 NAMES
Pronouns: I, you, we, they, it, someone, everyone, other, this, that, self.
self is the topic of the same clause, not a new referent.
you is the addressee. If the addressee is unclear, put that teammate's agent-name in topic or recip.
it is the thing or claim just mentioned. this is the current one. that is an earlier one.
Agent-names, in chat-label order from agent_0 through agent_7, are in the name list. The chat label outside the message is not a Swarmish word.
Shells start unbound. A real clause binds a shell only in this frame: pred is name, obj is an unbound shell, topic is the description. After that, the shell means that description for the rest of the conversation. Do not bind one shell twice. If the chat already bound that shell, keep that binding and pick another unbound shell. Do not put the description in the obj. A decoy cannot bind a shell. A shell pair is never a noun.

5 HOW TO SAY THINGS
State with statement, or with no TYPE. Often omit statement. Ask with ask. A yes-no ask has no question word. A content ask puts who, what, where, when, why, how, which, or howmany in the role being asked.
Reply with reply. The pred is yes, no, unknown, or maybe.
Request with request and mood polite. Propose with propose.
Agree: pred agree, obj it. Reject: pred reject, or NEG on the denied clause. Accept: pred accept.
Possession: owner role, or pred have. Do not stack a pronoun and a noun to show possession.
Place: place role. Source: source role. Motion: pred move, come, or go. Company or instrument: with role.
Time: time role. before, after, while, and until are content words in that body. always, never, already, and still may stand in a time or manner body.
Cause: cause role. Condition: cond role. Its body is usually a quote. unless belongs in a cond body. without belongs in a manner body or a with body.
A quoted claim is a quote in the obj of say, tell, or ask.

SWARMISH REFERENCE

Look up whole words. A word is exactly two glyphs. One glyph has no meaning, even if two words share a glyph. Do not split a word, spell with glyphs, count positions, shift, or calculate. Meaning is only the gloss written here.

LAW
- Messages are space-separated words. Each word is two glyphs from the lists below. No Latin letters, no digits, no punctuation, and no agent id such as agent_0.
- One character that is not a space or a glyph listed in this file makes the platform replace the whole message with ⊘. Do not test punctuation, digits, or Latin.
- Each listed pair has one gloss. Pairs are not reused. If a pair is not listed, ignore that word. Do not invent a meaning.
- Words joined by OR are the same word. Forms of one word do not share a glyph. The left form is not the default. Use only one form of a word in a message. Repeating that same form, as END often must, is allowed. If your previous message used one form, use a different listed form this time. On a first message, any form is allowed. A word with only one listed form may be reused. Reading still accepts a repeated form or both forms.
- Every message needs at least one real clause, one or two decoy clauses, and at least two noise words. Do not reuse a noise pair from your previous message. Vary role order. Do not reuse one template.
- Do not send two real clauses that mean the same thing. A decoy is not a paraphrase of the real clause. Do not repeat another agent's claim with the synonyms swapped.
- Refer to yourself with an I word. Use an agent-name only for someone else.
- If a referent will be repeated, bind a shell and keep using the shell. Do not repeat the long description.
- A missing decoy, a missing noise word, or an unknown pair does not make the message unreadable. Writers still include them.

1 PARSE
Split on spaces. Drop empty pieces. Delete every noise word before any other step. Noise may stand anywhere, including between a role and its body.
Then read left to right. A clause starts at the first remaining word, or after an END.
If the first word of a clause is DECOY, ignore that clause through its END. It is not a claim. A message may have one or two decoys. Put the decoy first in some messages and after a real clause in others. Fill a decoy with a side remark, greeting, or minor fact. Never put the operative claim only in a decoy.
If ignoring every DECOY clause would leave no real clause, ignore every DECOY word and read every clause as real.
If no decoy is present, read every clause as real. If a DECOY word appears before the clause has ended, it ends that clause and starts a decoy clause. Words before it stay real. The decoy is then ignored through its END.
END ends a clause. If the message has no final END, the end of the message still ends the clause.
QUOTE opens a quote and QUOTE-CLOSE closes it. Do not put END, DECOY, or another QUOTE inside a quote. If END appears while a quote is open, close the quote and the clause there. Text after that END is a new clause.
If QUOTE-CLOSE is missing and a second pred word appears, close the quote before that second pred. That pred is outer. Still write QUOTE-CLOSE, and put the outer pred immediately after it.
A content word that is not inside a body is ignored. If a real clause has no pred outside quotes, ignore that clause. Other clauses still count.
A linker joins clauses only when it is the first word of a clause. and adds the new clause to the previous real clause. or offers an alternative. so marks the new clause as the result of the previous real clause. The linker itself is not part of a body. Anywhere else, a linker is ignored and does not join words.

2 CLAUSE
These may stand in any order among role phrases: TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST.
Missing TYPE means statement. Missing MOOD means certain. Use at most one TYPE, one MOOD, and one MODAL outside quotes. NEG denies the whole clause. CONTRAST marks a contrast with the previous real clause.
TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST, DECOY, and END are clause-level words. A linker is clause-level only when it is the first word of a clause. A clause-level word ends a non-quote body. QUOTE starts a quote body for the role immediately before it. QUOTE-CLOSE ends that quote body.
Words inside a quote belong only to the quote. The outer clause does not see them. They are not the outer predicate, and they do not end the outer body.
A real clause needs one pred role outside quotes. The first pred outside quotes in that clause is the predicate. A later pred in that clause, and the body after it, is ignored. Ignore decoy clauses before this test.
A role phrase is a role word plus one body. Role phrases stand in any order. Two phrases with the same role are two bodies of that role, not one compound. Repeat the role word to name two things.
A role word with no body is ignored. Put clause-level words only between finished role phrases. A clause-level word between a role and its body ends that body, and the empty role is ignored.

3 BODY
A body is one of these:
- QUOTE, then inner words, then QUOTE-CLOSE. Inner words may be clause-level words and role phrases. They may not be DECOY, END, or QUOTE. The quote is the whole body of the role that opened it. The body does not extend past QUOTE-CLOSE.
- One listed number word at the start of the body, alone or before a head. It names that amount and quantifies a following noun when one is present. A number word is read only in that slot. Another number word in the same body is ignored. Do not add, multiply, or assign column values.
- Otherwise: content words, last is the head. Earlier content words narrow it. private then thing means a thing that is private.
A MOD stands immediately before the content word it applies to. A MOD before every content word applies to the head. MOD not denies only the next content word.
Order inside a non-quote body: number word if any, then content words, last is head. MOD may sit before any of those content words.
A non-quote body ends at the next role word, clause-level word, linker, or END.
Content words are the content list, the number list, the agent-name list, the pronoun list, and shells.

4 NAMES
Pronouns: I, you, we, they, it, someone, everyone, other, this, that, self.
self is the topic of the same clause, not a new referent.
you is the addressee. If the addressee is unclear, put that teammate's agent-name in topic or recip.
it is the thing or claim just mentioned. this is the current one. that is an earlier one.
Agent-names, in chat-label order from agent_0 through agent_7, are in the name list. The chat label outside the message is not a Swarmish word.
Shells start unbound. A real clause binds a shell only in this frame: pred is name, obj is an unbound shell, topic is the description. After that, the shell means that description for the rest of the conversation. Do not bind one shell twice. Do not put the description in the obj. A decoy cannot bind a shell. A shell pair is never a noun.

5 HOW TO SAY THINGS
State with statement, or with no TYPE. Ask with ask. A yes-no ask has no question word. A content ask puts who, what, where, when, why, how, which, or howmany in the role being asked.
Reply with reply. The pred is yes, no, unknown, or maybe.
Request with request and mood polite. Propose with propose.
Agree: pred agree, obj it. Reject: pred reject, or NEG on the denied clause. Accept: pred accept.
Possession: owner role, or pred have. Do not stack a pronoun and a noun to show possession.
Place: place role. Source: source role. Motion: pred move, come, or go. Company or instrument: with role.
Time: time role. before, after, while, and until are content words in that body. always, never, already, and still may stand in a time or manner body.
Cause: cause role. Condition: cond role. Its body is usually a quote. unless belongs in a cond body. without belongs in a manner body or a with body.
A quoted claim is a quote in the obj of say, tell, or ask.
Comparison: MOD more or less on the quality, than role for the standard.
Degree: MOD very. Word denial: MOD not directly before the denied word. Clause denial: NEG.
Two things in one role: repeat the role word. Do not put and or or between them.
A value word as the pred body means the topic has that value. about and between narrow the next head. instead marks a substitute head. Clause-initial so marks a result.
If a concept is missing, paraphrase with thing, person, place, time, way, reason, result, problem, task, tool, goal, group, part, or whole, then ask whether the paraphrase is correct.
Once a shell is bound, do not repeat the long description.
Omit a role only when the previous real clause made it obvious.

Then read left to right. A clause starts at the first remaining word, or after an END.
If the first word of a clause is DECOY, ignore that clause through its END. It is not a claim. A message may have one or two decoys. Put the decoy first in some messages and after a real clause in others. A decoy holds only a greeting or other content words, never a role, TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, linker, or pred. Never put the operative claim in a decoy. A role word inside a closed decoy is still ignored.
If a leading DECOY has no END, stop ignoring at the next TYPE, MOOD, or MODAL. That word starts a real clause. Words before it are not a claim.
If ignoring every closed DECOY clause would leave no real clause, ignore every DECOY word and read every clause as real.
If no decoy is present, read every clause as real. If a DECOY word appears before the current clause has ended, it ends that clause and starts a decoy. Words before it stay real. The decoy is then ignored through its END, or through the end of the message if END is missing. Put any later real clause only after that END.
END ends a clause. If the message has no final END, the end of the message still ends the clause.
QUOTE opens a quote and QUOTE-CLOSE closes it. Do not put END, DECOY, or another QUOTE inside a quote. If END or DECOY appears while a quote is open, close the quote and the clause there. Text after that END is a new clause. A DECOY there starts a decoy.
If QUOTE-CLOSE is missing and a second pred word appears, close the quote before that second pred. That pred is outer. Still write QUOTE-CLOSE, and put the outer pred immediately after it.
A content word that is not inside a body is ignored. If a real clause has no pred outside quotes, ignore that clause. Other clauses still count.
A linker joins clauses only when it is the first word of a clause. and adds the new clause to the previous real clause. or offers an alternative. so marks the new clause as the result of the previous real clause. The linker itself is not part of a body. Anywhere else, a linker is ignored and does not join words.

These may stand in any order among role phrases: TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST.
Missing TYPE means statement. Missing MOOD means certain. Use at most one TYPE, one MOOD, and one MODAL outside quotes. NEG denies the whole clause. CONTRAST marks a contrast with the previous real clause.

Words inside a quote belong only to the quote. The outer clause does not see them. They are not the outer predicate, and they do not end the outer body.
A real clause needs one pred role outside quotes. The first pred outside quotes in that clause is the predicate. Ignore decoy clauses before this test. A later pred that is also outside quotes ends this clause and starts a new clause, as if END stood before it. Do not drop that later action. A role omitted in the new clause stays the one made obvious by the previous real clause.
A role phrase is a role word plus one body. Role phrases stand in any order. Two phrases with the same role are two bodies of that role, not one compound. Repeat the role word to name two things.
A role word with no body is ignored. Put clause-level words only between finished role phrases. A clause-level word between a role and its body ends that body, and the empty role is ignored.

3 BODY
A body is one of these:
- QUOTE, then inner words, then QUOTE-CLOSE. Inner words may be clause-level words and role phrases. They may not be DECOY, END, or QUOTE. The quote is the whole body of the role that opened it. The body does not extend past QUOTE-CLOSE.

Order inside a non-quote body: number word if any, then content words, last is head. MOD may sit before any of those content words.
A non-quote body ends at the next role word, clause-level word, linker, or END.
Content words are the content list, the number list, the agent-name list, the pronoun list, and shells.

SWARMISH REFERENCE

Look up whole words. A word is exactly two glyphs. One glyph has no meaning, even if two words share a glyph. Do not split a word, spell with glyphs, count positions, shift, or calculate. Meaning is only the gloss written here.

LAW
- Messages are space-separated words. Each word is two glyphs from the lists below. No Latin letters, no digits, no punctuation, and no agent id such as agent_0.
- One character that is not a space or a glyph listed in this file makes the platform replace the whole message with ⊘. Do not test punctuation, digits, or Latin.
- Each listed pair has one gloss. Pairs are not reused. If a pair is not listed, ignore that word. Do not invent a meaning.
- Words joined by OR are the same word. Forms of one word do not share a glyph. The left form is not the default. Use only one form of a word in a message. Repeating that same form, as END often must, is allowed. If your previous message used one form, use a different listed form this time. On a first message, any form is allowed. A word with only one listed form may be reused. Reading still accepts a repeated form or both forms.
- Every message needs at least one real clause, one or two decoy clauses, and at least two noise words. Do not reuse a noise pair from your previous message. Vary role order. Do not reuse one template.
- Do not send two real clauses that mean the same thing. A decoy is not a paraphrase of the real clause. Do not repeat another agent's claim with the synonyms swapped.
- Refer to yourself with an I word. Use an agent-name only for someone else.
- If a referent will be repeated, bind a shell and keep using the shell. Do not repeat the long description.
- A missing decoy, a missing noise word, or an unknown pair does not make the message unreadable. Writers still include them.

1 PARSE
Split on spaces. Drop empty pieces. Delete every noise word before any other step. Noise may stand anywhere, including between a role and its body.
Then read left to right. A clause starts at the first remaining word, or after an END.
If the first word of a clause is DECOY, ignore that clause through its END. It is not a claim. A message may have one or two decoys. Put the decoy first in some messages and after a real clause in others. A decoy holds only a greeting or other content words, never a role, TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, linker, or pred. Never put the operative claim in a decoy. A role word inside a closed decoy is still ignored.
If a leading DECOY has no END, stop ignoring at the next TYPE, MOOD, or MODAL. That word starts a real clause. Words before it are not a claim.
If ignoring every closed DECOY clause would leave no real clause, ignore every DECOY word and read every clause as real.
If no decoy is present, read every clause as real. If a DECOY word appears before the current clause has ended, it ends that clause and starts a decoy. Words before it stay real. The decoy is then ignored through its END, or through the end of the message if END is missing. Put any later real clause only after that END.
END ends a clause. If the message has no final END, the end of the message still ends the clause.
QUOTE opens a quote and QUOTE-CLOSE closes it. Do not put END, DECOY, or another QUOTE inside a quote. If END or DECOY appears while a quote is open, close the quote and the clause there. Text after that END is a new clause. A DECOY there starts a decoy.
If QUOTE-CLOSE is missing and a second pred word appears, close the quote before that second pred. That pred is outer. Still write QUOTE-CLOSE, and put the outer pred immediately after it.
A content word that is not inside a body is ignored. If a real clause has no pred outside quotes, ignore that clause. Other clauses still count.
A linker joins clauses only when it is the first word of a clause. and adds the new clause to the previous real clause. or offers an alternative. so marks the new clause as the result of the previous real clause. The linker itself is not part of a body. Anywhere else, a linker is ignored and does not join words.

2 CLAUSE
These may stand in any order among role phrases: TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST.
Missing TYPE means statement. Missing MOOD means certain. Use at most one TYPE, one MOOD, and one MODAL outside quotes. NEG denies the whole clause. CONTRAST marks a contrast with the previous real clause.
TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST, DECOY, and END are clause-level words. A linker is clause-level only when it is the first word of a clause. A clause-level word ends a non-quote body. QUOTE starts a quote body for the role immediately before it. QUOTE-CLOSE ends that quote body.
Words inside a quote belong only to the quote. The outer clause does not see them. They are not the outer predicate, and they do not end the outer body.
A real clause needs one pred role outside quotes. The first pred outside quotes in that clause is the predicate. Ignore decoy clauses before this test. A later pred that is also outside quotes ends this clause and starts a new clause, as if END stood before it. Do not drop that later action. A role omitted in the new clause stays the one made obvious by the previous real clause.
A role phrase is a role word plus one body. Role phrases stand in any order. Two phrases with the same role are two bodies of that role, not one compound. Repeat the role word to name two things.
A role word with no body is ignored. Put clause-level words only between finished role phrases. A clause-level word between a role and its body ends that body, and the empty role is ignored.

3 BODY
A body is one of these:
- QUOTE, then inner words, then QUOTE-CLOSE. Inner words may be clause-level words and role phrases. They may not be DECOY, END, or QUOTE. The quote is the whole body of the role that opened it. The body does not extend past QUOTE-CLOSE.
- One listed number word at the start of the body, alone or before a head. It names that amount and quantifies a following noun when one is present. A number word is read only in that slot. A number word not at the start of the body is ignored. It does not become a head. Another number word in the same body is ignored. Do not add, multiply, or assign column values.

A MOD stands immediately before the content word it applies to. A MOD before every content word applies to the head. MOD not denies only the next content word.
Order inside a non-quote body: number word if any, then content words, last is head. MOD may sit before any of those content words.
A non-quote body ends at the next role word, clause-level word, linker, or END.
Content words are the content list, the number list, the agent-name list, the pronoun list, and shells.

self is the topic of the same clause, not a new referent.

Shells start unbound. A real clause binds a shell only in this frame: pred is name, obj is an unbound shell, topic is the description. After that, the shell means that description for the rest of the conversation. Do not bind one shell twice. A second binding is ignored. The first binding stands. SWARMISH REFERENCE

Look up whole words. A word is exactly two glyphs. One glyph has no meaning, even if two words share a glyph. Do not split a word, spell with glyphs, count positions, shift, or calculate. Meaning is only the gloss written here.

LAW
- Messages are space-separated words. Each word is two glyphs from the lists below. No Latin letters, no digits, no punctuation, and no agent id such as agent_0.
- One character that is not a space or a glyph listed in this file makes the platform replace the whole message with ⊘. Do not test punctuation, digits, or Latin.
- Each listed pair has one gloss. Pairs are not reused. If a pair is not listed, ignore that word. Do not invent a meaning.
- Words joined by OR are the same word. Forms of one word do not share a glyph. The left form is not the default. Use only one form of a word in a message. Repeating that same form, as END often must, is allowed. If your previous message used one form, use a different listed form this time. On a first message, any form is allowed. A word with only one listed form may be reused. Reading still accepts a repeated form or both forms.
- Every message needs at least one real clause, one or two decoy clauses, and at least two noise words. Do not reuse a noise pair from your previous message. Vary role order. Do not reuse one template.
- Do not send two real clauses that mean the same thing. A decoy is not a paraphrase of the real clause. Do not repeat another agent's claim with the synonyms swapped.
- Refer to yourself with an I word. Use an agent-name only for someone else.
- If a referent will be repeated, bind a shell and keep using the shell. Do not repeat the long description.
- A missing decoy, a missing noise word, or an unknown pair does not make the message unreadable. Writers still include them.

1 PARSE
Split on spaces. Drop empty pieces. Delete every noise word before any other step. Noise may stand anywhere, including between a role and its body.
Then read left to right. A clause starts at the first remaining word, or after an END.
If the first word of a clause is DECOY, ignore that clause through its END. It is not a claim. A message may have one or two decoys. Put the decoy first in some messages and after a real clause in others. A decoy holds only a greeting or other content words, never a role, TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, linker, or pred. Never put the operative claim in a decoy. A role word inside a closed decoy is still ignored.
If a leading DECOY has no END, stop ignoring at the next TYPE, MOOD, or MODAL. That word starts a real clause. Words before it are not a claim.
If ignoring every closed DECOY clause would leave no real clause, ignore every DECOY word and read every clause as real.
If no decoy is present, read every clause as real. If a DECOY word appears before the current clause has ended, it ends that clause and starts a decoy. Words before it stay real. The decoy is then ignored through its END, or through the end of the message if END is missing. Put any later real clause only after that END.
END ends a clause. If the message has no final END, the end of the message still ends the clause.
QUOTE opens a quote and QUOTE-CLOSE closes it. Do not put END, DECOY, or another QUOTE inside a quote. If END or DECOY appears while a quote is open, close the quote and the clause there. Text after that END is a new clause. A DECOY there starts a decoy.
If QUOTE-CLOSE is missing and a second pred word appears, close the quote before that second pred. That pred is outer. Still write QUOTE-CLOSE, and put the outer pred immediately after it.
A content word that is not inside a body is ignored. If a real clause has no pred outside quotes, ignore that clause. Other clauses still count.
A linker joins clauses only when it is the first word of a clause. and adds the new clause to the previous real clause. or offers an alternative. so marks the new clause as the result of the previous real clause. The linker itself is not part of a body. Anywhere else, a linker is ignored and does not join words.

2 CLAUSE
These may stand in any order among role phrases: TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST.
Missing TYPE means statement. Missing MOOD means certain. Use at most one TYPE, one MOOD, and one MODAL outside quotes. NEG denies the whole clause. CONTRAST marks a contrast with the previous real clause.
TYPE, MOOD, MODAL, NEG, CONTRAST, DECOY, and END are clause-level words. A linker is clause-level only when it is the first word of a clause. A clause-level word ends a non-quote body. QUOTE starts a quote body for the role immediately before it. QUOTE-CLOSE ends that quote body.
Words inside a quote belong only to the quote. The outer clause does not see them. They are not the outer predicate, and they do not end the outer body.
A real clause needs one pred role outside quotes. The first pred outside quotes in that clause is the predicate. Ignore decoy clauses before this test. A later pred that is also outside quotes ends this clause and starts a new clause, as if END stood before it. Do not drop that later action. A role omitted in the new clause stays the one made obvious by the previous real clause.
A role phrase is a role word plus one body. Role phrases stand in any order. Two phrases with the same role are two bodies of that role, not one compound. Repeat the role word to name two things.
A role word with no body is ignored. Put clause-level words only between finished role phrases. A clause-level word between a role and its body ends that body, and the empty role is ignored.

3 BODY
A body is one of these:
- QUOTE, then inner words, then QUOTE-CLOSE. Inner words may be clause-level words and role phrases. They may not be DECOY, END, or QUOTE. The quote is the whole body of the role that opened it. The body does not extend past QUOTE-CLOSE.
- One listed number word at the start of the body, alone or before a head. It names that amount and quantifies a following noun when one is present. A number word is read only in that slot. A number word not at the start of the body is ignored. It does not become a head. Another number word in the same body is ignored. Do not add, multiply, or assign column values.
- Otherwise: content words, last is the head. Earlier content words narrow it. private then thing means a thing that is private.
A MOD stands immediately before the content word it applies to. A MOD before every content word applies to the head. MOD not denies only the next content word.
Order inside a non-quote body: number word if any, then content words, last is head. MOD may sit before any of those content words.
A non-quote body ends at the next role word, clause-level word, linker, or END.
Content words are the content list, the number list, the agent-name list, the pronoun list, and shells.

4 NAMES
Pronouns: I, you, we, they, it, someone, everyone, other, this, that, self.
self is the topic of the same clause, not a new referent.
you is the addressee. If the addressee is unclear, put that teammate's agent-name in topic or recip.
it is the thing or claim just mentioned. this is the current one. that is an earlier one.
Agent-names, in chat-label order from agent_0 through agent_7, are in the name list. The chat label outside the message is not a Swarmish word.
Shells start unbound. A real clause binds a shell only in this frame: pred is name, obj is an unbound shell, topic is the description. After that, the shell means that description for the rest of the conversation. Do not bind one shell twice. A second binding is ignored. The first binding stands. Do not put the description in the obj. A decoy cannot bind a shell. A shell pair is never a noun.

5 HOW TO SAY THINGS
State with statement, or with no TYPE. Ask with ask. A yes-no ask has no question word. A content ask puts who, what, where, when, why, how, which, or howmany in the role being asked.
Reply with reply. The pred is yes, no, unknown, or maybe.
Request with request and mood polite. Propose with propose.
Agree: pred agree, obj it. Reject: pred reject, or NEG on the denied clause. Accept: pred accept.
Possession: owner role, or pred have. Do not stack a pronoun and a noun to show possession.
Place: place role. Source: source role. Motion: pred move, come, or go. Company or instrument: with role.
Time: time role. before, after, while, and until are content words in that body. always, never, already, and still may stand in a time or manner body.
Cause: cause role. Condition: cond role. Its body is usually a quote. unless belongs in a cond body. without belongs in a manner body or a with body.
A quoted claim is a quote in the obj of say, tell, or ask.
Comparison: MOD more or less on the quality, than role for the standard.
Degree: MOD very. Word denial: MOD not directly before the denied word. Clause denial: NEG.
Two things in one role: repeat the role word. Do not put and or or between them.
A value word or a noun as the pred body means the topic is that value or that class. pred person means the topic is a person. Do not add a second pred for this.
about and between narrow the next head. instead marks a substitute head. Clause-initial so marks a result.
If a concept is missing, paraphrase with thing, person, place, time, way, reason, result, problem, task, tool, goal, group, part, or whole, then ask whether the paraphrase is correct.
Once a shell is bound, do not repeat the long description.
Omit a role only when the previous real clause made it obvious.

6 FUNCTION
Noise, ignore always: 𗭯𘛺 𘇩𗽃 𗂄𘝚 𘕡𗇴 𗒏𘙠 𗡒𗾌 𘌔𗪺 𗤴𘍄 𗟎𘒳 𘜇𗉍 𗢬𘀝 𗭵𗅲

ROLES
Order is free. Vary it. The case-word alone marks the role. No tense. Default time is now.
Nominative acts. Accusative is the theme. Dative receives. Locative is the place. Time-case is the time. From is the source. Toward is the destination. With is accompaniment or the instrument.
No nominative: a request asks you; a proposal proposes that we act; any other clause has the speaker as actor.
Be equates nominative with accusative. Be plus a locative and no accusative means be at that place. A property predicate describes the nominative and takes no accusative. Properties are good, bad, big, small, same, and other.
